definition_en: to rest on the surface of a liquid, to move slowly in the air, to suggest an idea, or to let a currency change value freely
core_image: 一片叶子停在水面，随水波轻轻打转
scene: 一片叶子在水面上漂浮。 A leaf floated on the water.
sceneCN: 这里 float 是「漂浮」（第 1 个义项）；句意：一片叶子在水面上漂浮。

senses.title: Rest on liquid
senses.definition: to stay on the surface of water or another liquid
senses.definitionCN: 停留在水面或其他液体表面
senses.example: A leaf floated on the water.
senses.exampleCN: 一片叶子在水面上漂浮。
senses.why: This is the core physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心的物理义项。

senses.title: Move in air
senses.definition: to move slowly through the air without falling
senses.definitionCN: 缓慢地在空中移动而不下落
senses.example: A balloon floated over the trees.
senses.exampleCN: 一只气球飘过树梢。
senses.why: Air can hold things the way water does.
senses.whyCN: 空气能像水一样托住物体。

senses.title: Suggest an idea
senses.definition: to suggest an idea in order to test reaction
senses.definitionCN: 提出想法以试探反应
senses.example: She floated the idea of a new plan.
senses.exampleCN: 她提出了一个新计划的设想。
senses.why: An idea released for comment floats like a trial balloon.
senses.whyCN: 抛出征求意见的想法像试探气球一样飘起。

senses.title: Change freely
senses.definition: to let the value of a currency change with the market
senses.definitionCN: 让货币价值随市场变化
senses.example: The country let its currency float.
senses.exampleCN: 该国让货币自由浮动。
senses.why: A floating value is no longer tied down.
senses.whyCN: 浮动价值不再被固定住。

intro.en: Float comes from Old English flotian, from the same root as fleet and flow.
intro.cn: float 源自古英语 flotian，与 fleet、flow 同根。

items.en: The root meant to float or flow.
items.cn: 这个词根意为漂浮或流动。

items.en: Flotian meant to rest on water.
items.cn: flotian 意为停在水面上。

items.en: Float also named movement in air.
items.cn: float 也指在空中移动。

items.en: The verb came to mean proposing an idea.
items.cn: 这个动词开始指提出想法。

items.en: Economists used float for free currency values.
items.cn: 经济学家用 float 表示货币自由浮动。

note.en: Float is compared with similar-looking words and with words for drifting.
note.cn: 把 float 与形近词以及表示漂移的词作比较。

entries.definition: a group of ships
a musical instrument
having a level surface
to be carried slowly
to stay in the air
to move up and down

normalIntro.en: To float is to be held from below by water or air, and ideas can be floated too.
normalIntro.cn: float 就是被水或空气从下面托住，想法也可以被「托出来」试探。

normal.en: Wood floats on water.
normal.cn: 木头浮在水上。

normal.en: Clouds floated over the hill.
normal.cn: 云飘过山丘。

normal.en: He floated a new idea.
normal.cn: 他提出了一个新想法。

normal.en: The currency was allowed to float.
normal.cn: 货币被允许自由浮动。

normal.en: A float carried the band in the parade.
normal.cn: 游行彩车载着乐队。

abstract.en: Some things stay up only by moving with the current.
abstract.cn: 有些东西只有随流而动才能浮着。

abstract.en: An idea floated early can still sink later.
abstract.cn: 早早抛出的想法后来仍可能沉没。

abstract.en: Surface is a meeting point, not a wall.
abstract.cn: 表面是相遇之处，不是墙。

examples.en: A leaf floated on the water.
examples.cn: 一片叶子在水面上漂浮。

examples.en: A balloon floated over the trees.
examples.cn: 一只气球飘过树梢。

examples.en: She floated the idea of a new plan.
examples.cn: 她提出了一个新计划的设想。

dict_mnemonic.text: float 源自古英语 flotian（浮），与 flow 同根，核心义「被液体托住」，再引申为飘浮、试探性提出与货币浮动。

root: 源自古英语 flotian（漂浮），与 flow 同根，核心义「被流体托住而不下沉」。

sensesIntro.en: Float means to rest on liquid, to move in air, to suggest an idea, or to change freely.
sensesIntro.cn: float 意为漂浮、在空中飘、提出想法或自由浮动。

core.en: To be held up instead of sinking.
core.cn: 被托住而不下沉。

branches.en: Resting on the skin of water.
branches.cn: 停在水面上。

branches.en: Drifting slowly through air.
branches.cn: 在空气中缓慢飘移。

branches.en: An idea sent up for reaction.
branches.cn: 抛出去试探反应的想法。

branches.en: A value no longer tied down.
branches.cn: 不再被固定的价值。

branches.en: Water and air both carry things.
branches.cn: 水与空气都能承载物体。

intro.en: Float builds words for floating things, acts, and states.
intro.cn: float 构成表示漂浮物、动作和状态的词。

latinIntro.en: Float has no Latin ancestor; Latin fluctuare, to move in waves, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: float 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 fluctuare（波动）只是语义对应词。

items.example: A floating bridge crosses the river.

items.exampleCN: 一个漂浮物堵住了管道。

items.meaning: a plane that lands on water
items.example: The floatplane landed on the lake.

definition_en: to go under water, or to put something under water
core_image: 水面漫过头顶，一切声音都被压下去
scene: 洪水淹没了整条街道。 The flood submerged the whole street.
sceneCN: 这里 submerge 是「淹没」（第 1 个义项）；句意：洪水淹没了整条街道。

senses.title: Flood over
senses.definition: to cover something completely with water
senses.definitionCN: 用水把某物完全盖住
senses.example: The flood submerged the whole street.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水淹没了整条街道。
senses.why: This is the main physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是主要的物理义项。

senses.title: Go under
senses.definition: to go below the surface of water
senses.definitionCN: 沉到水面以下
senses.example: The submarine submerged quietly.
senses.exampleCN: 潜艇悄悄潜入水下。
senses.why: The same word works without an object.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也可不带宾语使用。

senses.title: Hide under
senses.definition: to be so involved that other things disappear
senses.definitionCN: 深陷其中，使其他事物仿佛消失
senses.example: She submerged herself in her work.
senses.exampleCN: 她把自己埋进工作里。
senses.why: Being under water images being lost in something.
senses.whyCN: 没入水中，被用来比喻沉浸在某事里。

intro.en: Submerge joins Latin sub, under, with mergere, to plunge.
intro.cn: submerge 由拉丁语 sub（在下）与 mergere（投入）组合而成。

items.en: Sub meant under.
items.cn: sub 意为在下。

items.en: Mergere meant to plunge into water.
items.cn: mergere 意为投入水中。

items.en: Submerge meant to put under water.
items.cn: submerge 意为把某物放入水下。

items.en: Submerge also meant to sink below the surface.
items.cn: submerge 也意为沉到水面以下。

items.en: Submerge gained the sense of being absorbed.
items.cn: submerge 获得了沉浸其中的含义。

note.en: Submerge is compared with look-alike words and with words for sinking.
note.cn: 把 submerge 与形近词以及表示下沉的词作比较。

to put under water
to put under water

to go down in water

normalIntro.en: To submerge is to go under, whether water or work.
normalIntro.cn: submerge 就是没入下面，无论是水还是工作。

normal.en: The flood submerged the whole street.
normal.cn: 洪水淹没了整条街道。

normal.en: The submarine submerged quietly.
normal.cn: 潜艇悄悄潜入水下。

normal.en: She submerged herself in her work.
normal.cn: 她把自己埋进工作里。

normal.en: The rocks were submerged at high tide.
normal.cn: 涨潮时岩石被水淹没。

normal.en: Do not submerge the pump in water.
normal.cn: 不要把水泵浸入水中。

abstract.en: Some feelings submerge and wait for a season.
abstract.cn: 有些情感会潜下去，等一个季节。

abstract.en: What is submerged still shapes the surface.
abstract.cn: 沉在水下的东西，仍在塑造水面。

abstract.en: To submerge is not to disappear.
abstract.cn: 没入水中，并不等于消失。

examples.en: The flood submerged the whole street.
examples.cn: 洪水淹没了整条街道。

examples.en: The submarine submerged quietly.
examples.cn: 潜艇悄悄潜入水下。

examples.en: She submerged herself in her work.
examples.cn: 她把自己埋进工作里。

dict_mnemonic.text: submerge 是「淹没、浸没」，也可表示「潜入水中」或「沉浸」；be submerged 是被淹没，fully submerged 是完全浸没，submerge oneself in 是沉浸于。

root: 由拉丁语 sub（在下）与 mergere（投入、浸入）组合，经法语或直接进入英语；字面是「投入到下面」，因此表示淹没、潜入水中，以及沉浸在某事里。

sensesIntro.en: Submerge means to flood over, to go underwater, or to be absorbed in something.
sensesIntro.cn: submerge 表示淹没、潜入水下，或沉浸于某事。

core.en: A surface closing over something.
core.cn: 水面在某物之上合拢。

branches.en: The flood submerged the whole street.
branches.cn: 洪水淹没了整条街道。

branches.en: The submarine submerged quietly.
branches.cn: 潜艇悄悄潜入水下。

branches.en: She submerged herself in her work.
branches.cn: 她把自己埋进工作里。

branches.en: Water covering a thing and a thing going under are two sides.
branches.cn: 水盖住东西，和东西沉下去，是同一件事的两面。

branches.en: Going underwater images being lost in a task.
branches.cn: 潜入水下，被用来比喻沉入一件事。

intro.en: Submerge takes -sion and -ible to build its family.
intro.cn: submerge 借助 -sion 和 -ible 构成同族词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base merg- meant to plunge.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 merg- 意为投入水中。

items.example: The tide will submerge the path.
The river submerges the field each spring.
items.exampleCN: 这条河每年春天淹没田地。
汽车有一部分被水淹没。

items.example: Submersion in cold water is dangerous.
The sun emerged from the clouds.

items.exampleCN: 语言沉浸有助于学习者。

latinEntries.example: Mergere gave English merge and submerge.
latinEntries.exampleCN: mergere 演变为英语的 merge 和 submerge。

definition_en: a machine with keys that prints letters on paper by striking a ribbon
core_image: 一排圆键被逐一按下，字杆弹起，在纸上留下一个字母
scene: 旧书房里，桌上摆着一台黑亮的机器，键帽已经磨白。 The typewriter still works after a hundred years.
sceneCN: 这里 typewriter 是「打字机」（第 1 个义项：通过按键击打色带在纸上印字的机器）；句意为这台打字机过了一百年仍能使用。字杆弹起、纸上留字的画面，就是这个词的样子。

derivatives.zh: 由 typewriter 反推的动词，义为「用打字机打字」
由 typewrite 加 -ing 构成，义为「打字机打字」
与 typewriter 同族，义为「打字员」

senses.title: The machine on the desk
senses.definition: a machine that prints letters on paper when its keys are struck
senses.definitionCN: 按下按键就能在纸上印出字母的机器
senses.example: The typewriter still works after a hundred years.
senses.exampleCN: 这台打字机过了一百年仍能使用。
senses.why: The word joins what it does: it writes letters of type.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把它的功能直接拼在一起：它写出活字字母。

senses.title: The way of writing it made
senses.definition: the style of writing that such machines produce
senses.definitionCN: 由这类机器产生的书写样式
senses.example: His early scripts were written in typewriter font.
senses.exampleCN: 他早期的剧本用的是打字机字体。
senses.why: A machine leaves its own look on the page, and that look acquired the name too.
senses.whyCN: 机器在纸上留下自己的样子，这种样子也拿到了这个名字。

intro.en: Typewriter is an English compound of type and writer, coined in America in the eighteen sixties.
intro.cn: typewriter 是 type 与 writer 的英语合成词，十九世纪六十年代造于美国。

items.en: Behind type stands typos, a stamp or the mark it leaves.
items.cn: type 背后是 typos，即印模或它留下的痕。

items.en: Typus and scriptor, a writer, meet in the Latin forms of the two halves.
items.cn: 两半的拉丁形式 typus 与 scriptor（书写者）在此相遇。

items.en: Early patents used the word for the person who typed as well as the machine.
items.cn: 早期专利里这个词既指打字的人，也指机器。

items.en: The machine sense won, and offices filled with keys and ribbons.
items.cn: 机器的意义获胜，办公室里满是按键与色带。

items.en: The keyboard survived the typewriter and kept the verb type.
items.cn: 键盘取代了打字机，却留下了动词 type。

note.en: The first group shares the type stem, the second names writing tools.
note.cn: 第一组共享 type 词干，第二组是书写工具。

entries.definition: Belonging to the machine.
Writing done on such a machine.
A device for receiving pictures.
A class, or to press keys.
A machine that puts ink on paper.
The set of keys.

normalIntro.en: Typewriter says what it is: a writer of types, letter by letter.
normalIntro.cn: typewriter 说的就是自己：一个写活字的书写者。

normal.en: Two words in one: type plus writer.
normal.cn: 两个词合成一个：type 加 writer。

normal.en: The plural is typewriters, with a single w.
normal.cn: 复数是 typewriters，只有一个 w。

normal.en: A typewriter has a ribbon, not a screen.
normal.cn: 打字机有色带，没有屏幕。

normal.en: The person who uses one is a typist.
normal.cn: 用打字机的人叫 typist。

normal.en: Its hour-long clatter is why writers could hear themselves think.
normal.cn: 它整小时的嗒嗒声，让写作者能听见自己在想什么。

abstract.en: A black machine under a dust cloth.
abstract.cn: 盖着防尘布的一台黑机器。

abstract.en: A bar of letters rising to strike a ribbon.
abstract.cn: 一排字杆扬起击在色带上。

abstract.en: One deep dent left on a sheet of paper.
abstract.cn: 纸页上留下的一处深深凹痕。

examples.en: She bought the typewriter at a street market.
examples.cn: 她在地摊上买下这台打字机。

examples.en: Every letter from the office had a typewriter mark.
examples.cn: 办公室里寄出的每封信都有打字机的凹痕。

examples.en: Computers replaced the typewriter but kept its keyboard.
examples.cn: 电脑取代了打字机，却保留了它的键盘。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「太普瑞特」——太普通的一篇文章，也要一个字一个字写出来，靠的是打字机。

root: 由 type（活字，本义为印痕）与 writer（书写者）合成的英语自造词，指用活字逐字击印的机器，同族词有 type、typist、typewriting。

sensesIntro.en: First the machine itself, then the written look it produced.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是机器本身，再是它造出的书写样子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a key pressing a bar against a ribbon.
core.cn: 核心意象：按下键让字杆打在色带上。

branches.en: The machine branch: metal and ink making letters.
branches.cn: 机器分支：金属与油墨造出字母。

branches.en: The style branch: the page keeps the machine's look.
branches.cn: 样式分支：纸页留着机器的样子。

branches.en: The workplace branch: offices run on such pages.
branches.cn: 职场分支：办公室靠这样的纸页运转。

branches.en: The writer branch: authors who type instead of write.
branches.cn: 写作者分支：用打字代替手写的作者。

branches.en: The font branch: a letterform borrowed from the machine.
branches.cn: 字体分支：从机器借来的字体。

intro.en: Typewriter is a two-part compound, and the family grows with -ing and -ist.
intro.cn: typewriter 是双部合成词，词族靠 -ing、-ist 扩展。

latinIntro.en: Its two Latin forebears are typus and scriptor, listed below.
latinIntro.cn: 它的两个拉丁先辈是 typus 与 scriptor，列在下面。

definition_en: a line of light, a strong horizontal bar, or a happy smile
core_image: 阳光从窗缝里斜射成一道光柱
scene: 门缝里漏进一道亮线。 A beam of light fell across the floor.
sceneCN: 这里 beam 是「光束」（第 1 个义项：成束射出的光线）；句意是一束光落在地板上。

derivatives.zh: 由 beam 加 -ing 构成，义为「喜气洋洋的」
由 sun 与 beam 复合，义为「阳光光束」

senses.title: A line of light
senses.definition: a narrow line of light
senses.definitionCN: 成束射出的细长光线
senses.example: A beam of light fell across the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 一束光落在地板上。
senses.why: Light was once pictured as a straight wooden beam, so the word moved to rays.
senses.whyCN: 人们曾把光线想象成笔直的木梁，于是这个词转指光线。

senses.title: A strong horizontal bar
senses.definition: a long strong bar that supports a building
senses.definitionCN: 支撑建筑的坚固长条材料
senses.example: Workers raised a steel beam into place.
senses.exampleCN: 工人把钢梁吊装到位。
senses.why: This was the older sense, from a word for a tree or plank.
senses.whyCN: 这是更早的义项，源头是表示树木或木板的词。

senses.title: To shine or smile widely
senses.definition: to shine brightly or to smile with pleasure
senses.definitionCN: 明亮地发光，或愉快地微笑
senses.example: She beamed at the good news.
senses.exampleCN: 听到好消息她笑了。
senses.why: The noun became a verb, first for shining light and then for a shining face.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词，先指发光，再指脸上放光般的笑容。

intro.en: Beam first meant a tree or plank, then a ray of light and a smile.
intro.cn: beam 最初指树木或木板，后来指光线与笑容。

items.en: beam meant a tree or a plank.
items.cn: beam 意为「树、木板」。

items.en: beam named a wooden support in a house.
items.cn: beam 指房屋中的木梁。

items.en: beam came to mean a ray of light.
items.cn: beam 开始指光线。

items.en: the verb meant to shine or smile.
items.cn: 动词义为发光或微笑。

items.en: beam covers light, timber and smiles.
items.cn: 如今 beam 兼指光线、木梁与笑容。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by one sound; the near-meaning group splits into light, timber and smiles.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个音；近义组分别对应光线、木梁与微笑。

normalIntro.en: A beam is a straight line of light, a strong bar, or a wide smile.
normalIntro.cn: beam 是笔直的光线、坚固的横梁，也是灿烂的笑容。

normal.en: The plural is beams.
normal.cn: 复数是 beams。

normal.en: A beam of light is a narrow line of light.
normal.cn: a beam of light 指一束窄光。

normal.en: A steel beam holds up a roof.
normal.cn: 钢梁支撑屋顶。

normal.en: Beam with joy means to smile widely.
normal.cn: beam with joy 指喜笑颜开。

normal.en: Sunbeam is sun plus beam.
normal.cn: sunbeam 是 sun 加 beam。

abstract.en: See light slanting through a crack.
abstract.cn: 想象光从缝隙斜射进来。

abstract.en: See a heavy bar across a ceiling.
abstract.cn: 想象横跨天花板的粗梁。

abstract.en: See a face lit by a wide smile.
abstract.cn: 想象一张被笑容照亮的脸。

examples.en: A beam of light fell across the floor.
examples.cn: 一束光落在地板上。

examples.en: Workers raised a steel beam into place.
examples.cn: 工人把钢梁吊装到位。

examples.en: She beamed at the good news.
examples.cn: 听到好消息她笑了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 beam 想成一根笔直的木梁，也可以是一道同样笔直的光。

root: 古英语 beam 本指树木或木板，中古英语指房屋木梁，十四世纪起因光线被想象成笔直的木条而转指光束，后又有「发光、微笑」的动词义。

sensesIntro.en: One straight shape serves for light, timber and a bright smile.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一种笔直的形态，贯穿光线、木梁与明朗的笑容。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: sunlight slanting through a window crack.
core.cn: 核心意象：阳光从窗缝斜射成柱。

branches.en: a narrow beam

branches.cn: 主梁

branches.cn: 喜笑颜开

intro.en: Beam takes -s, -ed and -ing, and joins sun in sunbeam.

definition_zh: 被动的；消极的；被动语态的；无动力的
definition_en: accepting what happens without active response or resistance, relating to the grammatical passive voice, or describing something that works without power or motion of its own
core_image: 一个人坐在长椅上，任身旁的人来来去去，自己始终没有起身
scene: 午后的公交站，一个人坐在长椅上，看着一班班车过去却始终没有起身。 He remained passive while the others argued about where to go.
sceneCN: 这里的 passive 是「消极的、不主动的」（第 1 个义项：不主动回应）；句意为别人争论要去哪里时，他始终不表态。图中可辨识物件：长椅、站牌、驶过的车。

pos.zh: 被动的；消极的；被动语态的；无动力的

derivatives.zh: 由 passive 加 -ly 构成，义为「被动地；消极地」
由 passive 加 -ity 构成，义为「被动；消极状态」
由否定前缀 im- 加 passive 构成，义为「无表情的；不动声色的」
由 passive 与 aggressive 复合而成，义为「消极对抗的」

senses.title: Accepting without active response
senses.definition: accepting what happens or what others do without acting, resisting or taking the initiative
senses.definitionCN: 对发生的事或别人的做法不作行动、不反抗、也不主动的
senses.example: He remained passive while the others argued about where to go.
senses.exampleCN: 别人争论要去哪里时，他始终不表态。
senses.why: Passive comes from the Latin word for suffering or undergoing, so the adjective first described someone who merely receives an action instead of starting one.
senses.whyCN: passive 来自拉丁语中表示「受苦、承受」的词，所以这个形容词最初形容只承受动作、不发起动作的人。

senses.title: Relating to the grammatical passive voice
senses.definition: describing a verb form or clause in which the subject receives the action rather than doing it
senses.definitionCN: 描述主语承受动作而不是发出动作的动词形式或从句
senses.example: The sentence was rewritten in the passive voice to sound more formal.
senses.exampleCN: 这个句子被改用被动语态，听起来更正式。
senses.why: Grammar borrowed the word because in a passive clause the subject is the one acted upon, exactly the role the adjective already named outside grammar.
senses.whyCN: 语法借用了这个词，因为在被动句里主语正是被作用的一方，这恰好就是形容词在语法之外早已指明的角色。

senses.title: Received from others rather than sought
senses.definition: describing something a person receives without acting, as in passive smoking or passive income
senses.definitionCN: 形容一个人并未主动争取而接受的东西，如被动吸烟或被动收入
senses.example: Children are most at risk from passive smoking at home.
senses.exampleCN: 儿童在家里受二手烟危害的风险最大。
senses.why: If the person is passive, whatever reaches them arrives without their effort, so smoking by others or money from investments is labelled passive from the receiver's side.
senses.whyCN: 如果人是被动的，那么来到他面前的一切都不是他努力得来的，于是别人吸烟或投资所得，都从接受者一方被叫作被动。

senses.title: Working without an outside power source
senses.titleCN: 无动力的；不消耗外部能源的
senses.definition: in technology, describing a device or system that works without an external power supply or moving parts
senses.definitionCN: 在技术领域，形容不靠外部电源或活动部件工作的装置或系统
senses.example: The building uses passive cooling instead of air conditioning.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋建筑采用被动式降温，而不使用空调。
senses.why: A passive component or a passive house simply sits there and lets physics do the work, so the old sense of receiving rather than acting fits machines as well as people.
senses.whyCN: 被动元件或被动式房屋只是待在那里，让物理规律去发挥作用，因此「承受而非施为」这个古老的意思，同样适用于机器。

intro.en: Passive comes from Latin passivus, capable of suffering or receiving an action, which was formed from the verb pati and reached English through Old French passif.
intro.cn: passive 来自拉丁语 passivus，意为「能受苦、能承受动作的」，由动词 pati 构成，经古法语 passif 进入英语。

items.en: Pati meant to suffer, to endure or to undergo, and it is the root behind passive, passion and patience.
items.cn: pati 意为受苦、忍受、承受，是 passive、passion 与 patience 共同的词根。

items.en: Passivus was a grammatical and philosophical term for what could receive an action rather than perform it.
items.cn: passivus 是语法与哲学用语，指能够承受动作而不是发出动作的东西。

items.en: Old French passif kept the sense of receiving and also named the passive voice in grammar.
items.cn: 古法语 passif 保留了「承受」之义，也用来指语法上的被动语态。

items.en: Middle English passive entered through grammar and philosophy, describing what is acted upon.
items.cn: 中古英语的 passive 经语法与哲学进入，形容被作用的一方。

items.en: Modern English extends the word to passive smoking, passive income and passive cooling, where no effort is made by the receiver.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词扩展到被动吸烟、被动收入与被动式降温，接受者都不必出力。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the Latin root for suffering; the near-meaning group collects words for people who do not act, with one direct opposite.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「受苦」词根上的词；近义组收表示不行动者的词，并收入一个直接的反义词。

entries.definition: A very strong feeling; both words come from Latin pati, to suffer.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈的情感；两词同出拉丁语 pati（受苦）。

entries.definition: The ability to endure waiting without complaint.
entries.definitionCN: 毫无怨言地忍受等待的能力。

entries.definition: Showing no emotion or reaction on the face.
entries.definitionCN: 脸上不显露情绪或反应的。

entries.definition: Sympathy for another person's suffering.
Not doing anything, or not working at the moment.
entries.definitionCN: 什么也不做，或暂时不运转的。

entries.definition: Willing to obey others without resistance.
entries.definitionCN: 愿意顺从他人而不反抗的。

entries.definition: Quiet and easy to control or teach.
entries.definitionCN: 安静、易于管束或教导的。

entries.definition: Doing things, taking initiative and making things happen.
entries.definitionCN: 做事、采取主动并推动事情发生的；passive 的反义词。

normalIntro.en: Passive is the grammar of receiving: its Latin root means to suffer or undergo, and the word keeps that shape whether it describes a person, a clause or a cooling system.
normalIntro.cn: passive 是「承受」的语法：它的拉丁词根意为受苦或承受，无论形容人、从句还是降温系统，这个词都保持这个形状。

normal.en: Passive and passion share the Latin root pati, to suffer: one is the state of being acted upon, the other is the feeling that comes with it.
normal.cn: passive 与 passion 共享拉丁词根 pati（受苦）：一个是承受动作的状态，一个是随之而来的情感。

normal.en: The passive voice puts the receiver first, which is why the object of an active sentence becomes the subject.
normal.cn: 被动语态把接受者放在前面，所以主动句的宾语变成了主语。

normal.en: Passive smoking is named from the non-smoker's side: the smoke arrives without being sought.
normal.cn: 被动吸烟是从不吸烟者一方命名的：烟是自己飘过来的，并非他去寻来的。

normal.en: Impassive is not passive plus a negative idea of weakness; it means the face shows nothing at all.
normal.cn: impassive 并不是「被动加懦弱」，它指脸上什么都不显露。

normal.en: Passive income still needs money or property behind it, so the word describes the receiver, not the absence of work.
normal.cn: 被动收入背后仍然需要资金或房产，所以这个词形容的是接受者，而不是没有付出。

abstract.en: A word whose root means to suffer reminds us that being acted upon is never entirely neutral.
abstract.cn: 一个词根意为「受苦」的词提醒人：被作用于身从来都不是完全中性的。

abstract.en: Grammar keeps a whole category for the receiver, which suggests that English finds it useful to say who was done to.
abstract.cn: 语法为接受者保留了一整个类别，这说明英语觉得说清「谁被怎么了」很有用。

abstract.en: A passive house and a passive person share one idea: letting forces already present do the work, for better or worse.
abstract.cn: 被动式房屋与被动的人共有一个想法：让已经存在的力量去发挥作用，无论好坏。

examples.en: He remained passive while the others argued about where to go.
examples.cn: 别人争论要去哪里时，他始终不表态。

examples.en: The sentence was rewritten in the passive voice to sound more formal.
examples.cn: 这个句子被改用被动语态，听起来更正式。

examples.en: Children are most at risk from passive smoking at home.
examples.cn: 儿童在家里受二手烟危害的风险最大。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「派西夫」——派西夫坐在长椅上一动不动，任事情自己发生；记住 passive 是被动的、消极的。

root: 来自拉丁语 passivus（能承受动作的），由动词 pati（受苦、承受）构成，经古法语 passif 进入英语；与 passion、patience 同根。

sensesIntro.en: The core is receiving rather than acting; the senses divide into a person who does not resist, the grammatical voice of the receiver, what arrives without being sought, and machines that work without power.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是承受而非施为；义项按「不反抗的人」「语法上接受者的语态」「不请自来的东西」「不耗动力的装置」分出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person sitting on a bench while others come and go, never standing up.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人坐在长椅上，任身旁的人来来去去，自己始终没有起身。

branches.en: a bench where someone never stands up
branches.cn: 始终没人站起来的一条长椅

branches.en: folded hands during an argument
branches.cn: 争论中交叠着的一双手

branches.en: a sentence turned around to face its object
branches.cn: 被调转过来朝向宾语的一个句子

branches.en: smoke drifting toward a child at a table
branches.cn: 飘向桌边孩子的一缕烟

branches.en: a house cooled by shade and stone
branches.cn: 靠阴影与石头降温的一所房子

intro.en: The word is the Latin adjective of receiving, made from the verb for suffering and a suffix meaning having the quality of.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语中表示「承受」的形容词，由表示受苦的动词与表示「具有……性质」的后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin pati and passivus are recorded, and Old French passif follows them, so the Latin ancestry of passive is reliable.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pati 与 passivus 均有记录，古法语 passif 紧随其后，因此 passive 的拉丁世系是可靠的。

definition_en: following one after another without a break
core_image: 日历一页页翻过去，每页都印着同样的雨
scene: 雨一连下了五天。 It rained for five successive days.
sceneCN: 这里 successive 是「连续的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：雨一连下了五天。

senses.title: Consecutive
senses.definition: following one after another with no break
senses.definitionCN: 一个接一个，中间没有间断
senses.example: It rained for five successive days.
senses.exampleCN: 雨一连下了五天。
senses.why: This is the main sense of things in a row.
senses.whyCN: 这是表示事物排成一串的主要义项。

senses.title: Succeeding
senses.definition: coming from one person or period to the next
senses.definitionCN: 从一个人或一个时期传到下一个

senses.why: Here one group takes over from the group before.

items.en: Successive now describes an unbroken series.

note.en: Successive is compared with look-alike words and with words for repeated order.

definition_en: in a way that shows pleasure and satisfaction in what one has done, in a way that shows too high an opinion of oneself, or in a way that stands out boldly
core_image: 一个人挺直背站在人群前面，下巴微微抬起，眼睛发亮
scene: 女儿把奖状举到胸前，母亲站在旁边，背挺得笔直，见人就说这是孩子自己挣来的。 The mother spoke proudly of her daughter's first prize.
sceneCN: 这里表示「自豪地」（第 1 个义项：因成绩或亲人而心里发亮）；句意为母亲一说起女儿得的一等奖，语气里全是自豪。

derivatives.zh: 本词的基础形容词，加上 -ly 即构成 proudly，义为「自豪的；骄傲的」
同族名词，与 proud 同出一源，义为「自豪；骄傲；自尊」
由 pride 加形容词后缀 -ful 构成，义为「骄傲的；自视过高的」

senses.title: In a way that shows pleasure in an achievement
senses.definition: in a way that shows you feel pleased and satisfied about something you or people close to you have done
senses.definitionCN: 表现出对自己或亲近之人所做成的事感到满意、心里发亮
senses.example: She proudly showed us the letter her son had written.
senses.exampleCN: 她自豪地把儿子写的信拿给我们看。
senses.why: Proud first described a person of worth and standing, and -ly turns that standing into a manner, so proudly is how someone carries a good result.
senses.whyCN: proud 最初形容一个人有分量、站得住，-ly 把这种站位变成举止方式，所以 proudly 就是一个人带着好成绩走路的样子。

senses.title: In a way that shows too high an opinion of oneself
senses.definition: in a way that shows you believe you are better than the people around you
senses.definitionCN: 表现出自认比周围的人高一等
senses.example: He proudly refused the advice of every older worker.
senses.exampleCN: 他傲慢地拒绝了每一位老工人的劝告。
senses.why: The same high standing can be earned or merely assumed, and when nothing was earned the manner turns into arrogance, so the adverb carries both praise and blame.
senses.whyCN: 同样一种「站得高」，可以是挣来的，也可以是自己假定的；当它并非挣来，这种举止就变成傲慢，所以这个副词既带称赞也带责备。

senses.title: In a way that rises or stands out boldly
senses.definition: used of a building, a ship or a feature that rises or shows itself in a bold, dignified way
senses.definitionCN: 用于建筑、船只或某处特征，指其挺拔、醒目而体面地立在那里
senses.example: The old tower stands proudly above the harbour.
senses.exampleCN: 那座旧塔傲然立在港湾之上。
senses.why: English lends the human posture to things: whatever rises straight and refuses to hide seems to hold its head up, so a tower can stand proudly.
senses.whyCN: 英语把人的姿态借给了物：凡是笔直立起、又不肯躲藏的，就像抬着头一样，于是塔也能 stand proudly。

intro.en: Proudly is an English-made adverb from proud, a word that came through French and is generally traced to a Late Latin sense of being useful or of value.
intro.cn: proudly 是英语内部由 proud 加 -ly 造出的副词；proud 经法语而来，一般认为可追到晚期拉丁语中「有用、有价值」的意思。

items.en: The Latin verb prodesse meant to be useful or to do good, and a thing that is useful can be counted as worth something.
items.cn: 拉丁动词 prodesse 意为有用、带来好处；有用的东西自然被视为有价值。

items.en: The adjective prode meant useful, profitable or brave, and it is generally cited as the starting point of the French word.
items.cn: 形容词 prode 意为有用的、有利的、勇敢的，一般认为这是法语那个词的起点。

items.en: Old French prou or prud described someone brave, worthy and of good standing.
items.cn: 古法语 prou 或 prud 形容一个人勇敢、可敬、有地位。

items.en: Middle English proud could mean brave and magnificent as well as having a high opinion of oneself.
items.cn: 中古英语 proud 既能表示勇敢、气派，也能表示自视甚高。

items.en: Modern English keeps both sides, so proud is praise in a parent's mouth and blame in a critic's, and -ly turns each into a manner.
items.cn: 现代英语把两面都留下：在父母嘴里 proud 是称赞，在批评者嘴里是责备，而 -ly 把这两种都变成举止方式。

note.en: The first group is the small family of pride words, including one that only looks alike; the second group gathers adverbs for feeling good about oneself.
note.cn: 第一组是与「自豪」有关的小词族，其中一个只是看起来像；第二组收表示「对自己感觉良好」的副词。

entries.definition: The adjective behind the adverb: feeling pleased, or thinking too well of oneself.
entries.definitionCN: 本词所依附的形容词：感到自豪，或自视过高。

entries.definition: The noun for that feeling; it also names a group of lions.
entries.definitionCN: 这种感觉的名词；也指一群狮子。

entries.definition: To push with a finger or a stick; only the spelling is close, the origin is unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 用手指或棍子戳；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: In a way that shows you think you are better than others.
In a cold and superior manner.
In a way that shows belief in oneself or in one's judgment.
entries.definitionCN: 表现出对自己或自己的判断有信心。

entries.definition: In an impressive and self-important manner.

normalIntro.en: The adverb adds a manner to a word about standing tall: whoever is proud holds the body, and the voice, a little higher than usual.
normalIntro.cn: 这个副词给「站得高」这个词添上了举止：心里自豪的人，身体和声音都会比平常抬高一点。

normal.en: Proudly is simply proud plus -ly, so the adverb is the adjective's posture turned into a way of speaking or standing.
normal.cn: proudly 就是 proud 加 -ly，所以这个副词是形容词的姿态变成了说话或站立的方式。

normal.en: Pride is the noun of the same feeling; the pair pride and proud is irregular in shape but regular in meaning.
normal.cn: pride 是同一份感觉的名词；pride 与 proud 形式不整齐，意思却一一对应。

normal.en: The old sense of proud as brave explains why a tower or a ship can stand proudly: that is height, not vanity.
normal.cn: proud 古有「勇敢、气派」之义，这解释了塔或船为何能 stand proudly：那是高度，不是虚荣。

normal.en: A parent's proudly and a critic's proudly sound the same, and only the situation tells praise from blame.
normal.cn: 父母嘴里的 proudly 与批评者嘴里的 proudly 发音相同，只有情境能分出称赞与责备。

normal.en: The -ly ending is native English, so proudly was built inside the language from an adjective borrowed through French.
normal.cn: -ly 是英语本族词尾，所以 proudly 是用一个经法语借来的形容词在英语内部造出来的。

abstract.en: Pride lifts the body, and the adverb records that lift in the shoulders and in the voice.
abstract.cn: 自豪会把身体抬起，这个副词记录的就是肩膀与声音里的那一下抬起。

abstract.en: One manner serves both self-respect and vanity because the outside looks the same, and only the inside differs.
abstract.cn: 同一种举止既用于自尊也用于虚荣，因为外表一样，差别只在里面。

abstract.en: To speak proudly is to let others see how much a thing matters to you, which is a small act of exposure.
abstract.cn: 自豪地说，就是让别人看见某件事对你有多重要，这是一种小小的袒露。

examples.en: She proudly introduced her father to the class.
examples.cn: 她自豪地把父亲介绍给全班。

examples.en: The team proudly displayed the trophy in the hall.
examples.cn: 球队把奖杯自豪地摆在大厅里。

examples.en: He proudly ignored the warnings of his friends.
examples.cn: 他傲慢地不理会朋友们的提醒。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑劳德利」——胸脯一挺，声音就跟着亮起来；记住 proudly 是自豪地、骄傲地。

root: proudly 由形容词 proud 加副词后缀 -ly 构成。proud 经古法语 prou、prud 进入英语，一般认为更早可追到晚期拉丁语 prode（有用的、有价值的），再往前是 prodesse（有益）。所以这个词的起点不是「骄傲」，而是「有分量、有价值」。英语里 pride 是同一族的名词。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a body held higher than usual; the senses divide into earned satisfaction, unearned superiority, and the borrowed posture of tall things.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「比平常抬得更高的身体」；义项由此分出挣来的满足、没挣来的优越，以及借给高耸之物的那种姿态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person standing straight with the chin slightly raised and the eyes bright.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人挺直站着，下巴微微抬起，眼睛发亮。

branches.en: a prize held against the chest
branches.cn: 奖状贴在胸前

branches.en: a chin raised at advice that is refused
branches.cn: 拒绝劝告时抬起的下巴

branches.en: a tower above the harbour
branches.cn: 港湾上方的一座塔

branches.en: height that is earned and height that is only built
branches.cn: 挣来的高度与只是造出来的高度

branches.en: one posture for pride and for stone
branches.cn: 一种姿态，既属于骄傲也属于石头

intro.en: A Late Latin adjective of worth, its French descendant, and the native English -ly that turns an adjective into a manner hold the word together.
intro.cn: 表示「有价值」的晚期拉丁语形容词、它在法语里的后身，以及把形容词变成举止的英语本族词尾 -ly，共同支撑这个词。

latinIntro.en: Prode and prodesse are the Latin forms usually cited, while the French stage of the journey is the part that is certain.
latinIntro.cn: prode 与 prodesse 是通常引用的拉丁语形式；可以确定的是它经法语传来的那一段。

items.meaning: to be useful, to do good
having a high opinion of oneself

latinEntries.meaning: to be useful, to do good

definition_zh: 安装；装置；（艺术）装置作品
definition_en: the act of putting equipment in place, the equipment itself, or a large artistic structure
core_image: 一整套机器已经安好，电缆整齐地排进墙槽，旁边贴着验收单
scene: 厂房一角新刷过漆，地面还留着包装箱的印子。 The installation of the new pumps took the whole weekend.
sceneCN: 这里 installation 是「安装」（第 1 个义项：把设备安置到位的动作），句意是新水泵的安装花了整个周末。画面里能看到的物件：电缆、墙槽、验收单、包装箱印子。

pos.zh: 名词：安装；装置；装置艺术品

derivatives.zh: 本词所对应的动词，义为「安装；使就职」
由动词加 -er 构成，义为「安装者；安装程序」
由本词加 -al 构成，义为「与安装有关的」

senses.title: The act of installing
senses.definition: the process of fixing equipment or software in place and making it ready to use
senses.definitionCN: 把设备或软件固定到位并使其可用的过程
senses.example: The installation of the lift will close the stairs for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 装电梯期间楼梯要封闭一周。
senses.why: The noun of action -ation turns the verb into the process itself.
senses.whyCN: 行为名词词尾 -ation 把动词变成「过程」本身。

senses.title: The equipment installed
senses.definition: the machines, wiring, or system that has been put in place
senses.definitionCN: 已经安装到位的机器、线路或系统
senses.example: The fire alarm installation must be tested twice a year.
senses.exampleCN: 火警装置必须每年检测两次。
senses.why: The result is named by the same word as the act: the thing installed is an installation.
senses.whyCN: 结果与行为用同一个词：装好的东西也是一项 installation。

senses.title: A large work of art arranged in a space
senses.definition: a work of art made of objects placed in a room or landscape that the viewer walks through
senses.definitionCN: 由物件布置在房间或景观中、观众可以走进去的艺术作品
senses.example: The gallery bought a light installation that fills the whole hall.
senses.exampleCN: 画廊买下了一件占满整个大厅的灯光装置作品。
senses.why: Twentieth-century artists began to install objects rather than hang them, and named the result an installation.
senses.whyCN: 二十世纪艺术家开始「安装」物件而非悬挂画作，并把成果称作 installation。

intro.en: Installation is the Latin noun of action on installare "to put into a seat", the same stem as install.
intro.cn: installation 是拉丁语 installare「放入座位」的行为名词，与 install 同一词干。

items.en: Stallum "stall, seat" and installare "to place in a seat" are medieval church terms.
items.cn: stallum「座位」与 installare「放入座位」都是中世纪教会用语。

items.en: The ending -atio formed nouns of action from verbs throughout Latin.
items.cn: 词尾 -atio 在拉丁语中广泛把动词变成行为名词。

items.en: Old French installation and installer carried both to English.
items.cn: 古法语 installation 与 installer 把两者都带入英语。

items.en: By the nineteenth century the word covered factories, ships and railways.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，这个词已涵盖工厂、船舶与铁路。

items.en: After the nineteen sixties it also named room-sized works of art.
items.cn: 二十世纪六十年代以后，它又指占据房间的艺术作品。

note.en: The look-alike group is the install family; the near-meaning group holds other words for installed systems and arranged art.
note.cn: 形近组是 install 词族；近义组收其他表示「装好的系统」与「布置艺术」的词。

entries.definition: The verb that names what the installation does.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，即 installation 所指的动作。

entries.definition: The person or program that performs the installation.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指执行安装的人或程序。

entries.definition: A booth or seat, the literal place inside the word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「摊位、座位」，是词内字面的位置。

entries.definition: The arrangement of equipment, used informally.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「设置、装置」，口语常用。

entries.definition: The machines themselves, without reference to fitting them.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「设备」，不涉及安装动作。

entries.definition: Something shown in a gallery, including installations.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「展品」，可包括装置作品。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the -ation ending and the three things the word can mean.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子利用 -ation 词尾以及这个词可以指代的三类事物。

normal.en: Install plus -ation: the act, then the thing, then the art.
normal.cn: install 加 -ation：先是动作，再是设备，再是艺术。

normal.en: Installation costs are separate from the price of the machine.
normal.cn: 安装费与机器价格是分开的。

normal.en: Software installation should not take an afternoon.
normal.cn: 软件安装不该花掉一下午。

normal.en: A fire alarm installation is tested twice a year.
normal.cn: 火警装置每年检测两次。

normal.en: An art installation may be a room you walk into.
normal.cn: 装置艺术可能是一间你走进去的房间。

abstract.en: An installation is order made visible on a wall.
abstract.cn: 安装是秩序在墙上的可见化。

abstract.en: The same word names the doing and the done.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指「做」，也指「做成」。

abstract.en: Walking through an installation, you become part of it.
abstract.cn: 走过装置艺术品时，你也成了它的一部分。

examples.en: The installation of the new lines will begin in May.
examples.cn: 新线路的安装将在五月开始。

examples.en: The museum owns a huge sound installation.
examples.cn: 这座博物馆藏有一件巨大的声音装置作品。

examples.en: Check the installation before you switch it on.
examples.cn: 开机之前先检查安装情况。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬装类事」——硬装这一类事，就是安装

root: 中世纪拉丁语 stallum「座位、摊位」→ installare「放入座位」→ 拉丁行为名词词尾 -atio → 古法语 installation → 英语 installation。与 install、installer 同族，二十世纪又引申指装置艺术。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: the process, the finished equipment, and a work of art that occupies a space.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：安装过程、装好的设备，以及占据空间的装置艺术品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: machines sit in place with neat wiring, a signed form taped to the wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：机器就位、布线整齐，墙上贴着一张签好的单子。

branches.en: THE WORK: the weekend spent fitting the pumps.
branches.cn: 施工这条线：整个周末装水泵的过程。

branches.en: THE ROOM: the finished equipment is itself an installation.
branches.cn: 房间这条线：装好的设备本身就是一项 installation。

branches.en: THE GALLERY: objects arranged in a space as art.
branches.cn: 画廊这条线：把物件布置在空间中的艺术。

branches.en: THE LINK: act and result share one word, as with many -ation nouns.
branches.cn: 连接线：动作与结果共用一个词，许多 -ation 名词皆如此。

branches.en: THE SHIFT: the art sense borrows the industrial word for its own purposes.
branches.cn: 转义线：艺术义借用了工业词汇。

intro.en: Installation is install- plus the Latin noun ending -ation, parallel to station and situation.
intro.cn: installation 是 install- 加拉丁名词词尾 -ation，与 station、situation 同构。

latinIntro.en: Stallum, installare and the ending -atio are all attested in medieval Latin.
latinIntro.cn: stallum、installare 与词尾 -atio 在中世纪拉丁语中均有记载。

items.example: Installational belongs to a rare register.
The verb is shorter and plainer.
The agent noun of the same stem.

items.exampleCN: 不带前缀的名词仍在用。

items.example: A sister noun from the same idea of standing.
items.exampleCN: 同义「站立处」的姊妹名词。

definition_en: to press something into a smaller space, or to make speech or writing shorter
core_image: 双手把一团棉花使劲压成硬硬的一小块
scene: 打包行李时，她把毛衣卷紧塞进箱角。 She managed to compress the sleeping bag into a small sack.
sceneCN: 这里 compress 指「压缩」（第 1 个义项：把东西压进更小的空间）；句意是她设法把睡袋压进一个小袋子里。

senses.title: Press into less space
senses.definition: to press something so that it takes up less space
senses.definitionCN: 按压某物，使它占据更小的空间
senses.example: The machine compresses the wool into bales.
senses.exampleCN: 这台机器把羊毛压成捆。
senses.why: Force closes the gaps between fibres, and the same mass fits a smaller box.
senses.whyCN: 力量挤掉纤维间的空隙，同样的质量就装进更小的箱子。

senses.title: Make shorter
senses.definition: to make speech or writing shorter while keeping the main points
senses.definitionCN: 在保留要点的前提下使讲话或文字更短
senses.example: He compressed the report into two pages.
senses.exampleCN: 他把报告压缩成了两页。
senses.why: Words, like wool, carry empty space that can be pressed out.
senses.whyCN: 文字和羊毛一样带着可被挤掉的空间。

senses.title: A cloth pressed on the body
senses.definition: a cloth pressed against part of the body to reduce heat or stop bleeding
senses.definitionCN: 压在身体某部位以降热或止血的布
senses.example: Apply a cold compress to the bruise.
senses.exampleCN: 在淤伤处敷一块冷布。
senses.why: The cloth is literally pressed down, so the noun keeps the same picture.
senses.whyCN: 这块布确实被压下去，所以名词保留了同一幅画面。

intro.en: Compress comes from Latin comprimere, to press together, and first described physical squeezing.
intro.cn: compress 来自拉丁语 comprimere（压在一起），最初描述物理上的挤压。

items.en: Com- meant together and premere meant to press.
items.cn: com- 表示一起，premere 表示压。

items.en: Comprimere described pressing something into a tight mass.
items.cn: comprimere 描述把某物压成紧密的一团。

items.en: Old French compresser kept the physical sense of squeezing.
items.cn: 古法语 compresser 保留了挤压的具体含义。

items.en: English compress first meant to squeeze or to press down.
items.cn: 英语 compress 最初指挤压或按压。

items.en: It now also covers shortening text and shrinking computer files.
items.cn: 如今它也指缩短文字与缩小电脑文件。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words sharing the shape of compress, and the meaning group names other ways of making something smaller.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 compress 形状相近的词，近义组列出其他使东西变小的说法。

entries.definition: the act of pressing something smaller
a machine that compresses air or gas
to stop something by force
to press something firmly from both sides
to make something shorter or thicker
to make something less long

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with wool forced into a bale, then move to shortened reports and to a cold cloth.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从被压成捆的羊毛开始，再走到缩短的报告与一块冷布。

normal.en: Com- is together and press is to squeeze, so compress is to squeeze together.
normal.cn: com- 是一起，press 是挤，compress 就是挤到一起。

normal.en: A compressed file takes less room on a disk.
normal.cn: 压缩过的文件在磁盘上占的地方更小。

normal.en: A cold compress is a cloth that presses down on a bruise.
normal.cn: 冷敷布就是压在淤伤上的一块布。

normal.en: Compress a long story and only the bones remain.
normal.cn: 把长故事压缩后，只剩下了骨架。

normal.en: The opposite is decompress, to let the air back in.
normal.cn: 反义词是 decompress，也就是让空气重新进去。

abstract.en: Picture a thick blanket rolled tight enough to tie.
abstract.cn: 想象一床厚毯子被卷紧到可以捆起来。

abstract.en: Picture a page of notes folded into a pocket.
abstract.cn: 想象一页笔记被折进衣袋。

abstract.en: Picture two hands pushing a spring flat.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手把一根弹簧压平。

examples.en: The pump compresses air into the tank.
examples.cn: 泵把空气压进罐里。

examples.en: She compressed her notes into a single page.
examples.cn: 她把笔记压缩成了一页。

examples.en: Hold the compress against the wound for five minutes.
examples.cn: 把敷布按在伤口上五分钟。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 compress 记成 com（一起）加 press（压）：把东西压到一起，就是压缩。

root: 源自拉丁语 comprimere（com 一起 + premere 压），本义是压紧、挤压，后引申为简缩文字与压缩文件，并作名词指敷布。

sensesIntro.en: From wool pressed into a bale, to words pressed into a page, and finally to a cloth pressed on the skin.
sensesIntro.cn: 从羊毛被压成捆，到文字被压成一页，最后到压在皮肤上的布。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands forcing a ball of cotton into a hard little lump.
core.cn: 核心意象：双手把一团棉花压成硬硬的一小块。

branches.en: Physical squeezing is the oldest and clearest sense.
branches.cn: 物理挤压是最古老也最清楚的义项。

branches.en: Shortening text is squeezing words instead of wool.
branches.cn: 缩短文字，挤的是词而不是羊毛。

branches.en: The medical noun keeps the literal picture of a cloth pressed down.
branches.cn: 医学名词保留了布被压下去的字面画面。

branches.en: Both senses remove empty space and keep the substance.
branches.cn: 两个义项都去掉空隙，留下实质。

branches.en: A machine and a nurse both apply steady pressure.
branches.cn: 机器和护士都在施加稳定的压力。

intro.en: Compress is built on Latin com-, together, plus premere, to press.
intro.cn: compress 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 premere（压）构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin press base also gives pressure, express and impress.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的压力词基还给出 pressure、express 与 impress。

items.example: The device compresses the gas quickly.
items.exampleCN: 这个装置迅速压缩气体。

items.example: The file is compressed for sending.
items.exampleCN: 文件已被压缩以便发送。

items.meaning: the act or result of pressing
items.example: The compression of the spring stores energy.
items.exampleCN: 弹簧的压缩储存了能量。

items.example: The material has high compressive strength.

definition_en: a hard pointed growth on an animal, or a device that makes a warning sound
core_image: 一头公牛低头时弯弯的尖角
scene: 那头公牛的角又长又尖。 The bull has long, sharp horns.
sceneCN: 这里 horn 是「动物的角」（第 1 个义项）；句意：那头公牛的角又长又尖。

senses.title: An animal's hard growth
senses.definition: a hard pointed growth on the head of an animal
senses.definitionCN: 动物头上坚硬而尖的突出物
senses.example: The bull has long, sharp horns.
senses.exampleCN: 那头公牛的角又长又尖。
senses.why: This is the basic bodily sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的身体部位义项。

senses.title: A warning device
senses.definition: a device on a vehicle that makes a loud sound
senses.definitionCN: 车辆上发出响亮声音的装置
senses.example: She honked the horn at the crossing.
senses.exampleCN: 她在路口按了喇叭。
senses.why: The device borrows the shape and the sound.
senses.whyCN: 这个装置借用了角的形状与声响。

senses.title: A brass instrument
senses.definition: a simple brass instrument played by blowing
senses.definitionCN: 靠吹奏发声的简单铜管乐器
senses.example: A hunter blew a horn in the distance.
senses.exampleCN: 远处有猎人吹响号角。
senses.why: This is the old musical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是古老的乐器义项。

intro.en: Horn is one of the oldest Germanic words, naming the hard growth on an animal.
intro.cn: horn 是最古老的日耳曼语词之一，指动物头上坚硬的角。

items.en: Hurnam meant horn.
items.cn: hurnam 意为角。

items.en: Horn meant a horn.
items.cn: horn 意为角。

items.en: Horn meant an animal horn or a trumpet.
items.cn: horn 指兽角或号角。

items.en: Horn named car horns and tools.
items.cn: horn 指汽车喇叭与工具。

items.en: It formed horned and shoehorn.
items.cn: 它构成了 horned 和 shoehorn。

note.en: Horn is compared with look-alike words and with words for animal growths and trumpets.
note.cn: 把 horn 与形近词以及表示兽角、号角的词作比较。

damaged by use

normalIntro.cn: horn 指动物头上坚硬的角，也指用角做成、能发出响声的东西。

normal.cn: 她在路口按了喇叭。

normal.en: A hunter blew a horn in the distance.
normal.cn: 远处有猎人吹响号角。

normal.en: A deer raised its head and showed its horns.

abstract.en: A horn is a bone that learned to speak.
abstract.cn: 角，是一根学会发声的骨头。

abstract.en: What protects can also warn.
abstract.cn: 用来保护的东西，也能用来警告。

abstract.en: Old horns still call across new valleys.
abstract.cn: 古老的号角，仍能越过新的山谷呼唤。

definition_zh: 迅速地；立即；准时地；干脆地
definition_en: in a quick and immediate way, or exactly at the arranged time
core_image: 指针刚跳到约定的那一格，人已经站在门口，东西也都准备好了
scene: 邮局刚开门，柜台前的人就把一叠信递上去，说这些都得当天寄出。 She answered the letter promptly and posted it the same morning.
sceneCN: 这里表示「迅速地、立即」（第 1 个义项：几乎没有拖延就做出反应）；句意为她很快回了信，并在当天上午寄了出去。

pos.zh: 迅速地；立即；准时地；干脆地

derivatives.zh: promptly 的基础词，义为「迅速的；促使」
由 prompt 加 -ness 构成，义为「迅速；及时」
由 prompt 加 -ing 构成，义为「提示；鼓励」

senses.title: Without delay; at once
senses.definition: in a way that happens at once, with almost no gap between the cause and the response
senses.definitionCN: 事情立刻发生，起因与反应之间几乎没有间隔
senses.example: The nurse answered the bell promptly.
senses.exampleCN: 护士听到铃声立刻应了。
senses.why: The adjective described something ready at hand, and -ly turns that readiness into the manner of an action: nothing has to be fetched first.
senses.whyCN: 形容词本指「就在手边、随时可用」，-ly 把这份现成变成动作的方式：不必先去取什么。

senses.title: Exactly at the agreed time
senses.definition: at the stated time and not later, so that an appointment or timetable is kept
senses.definitionCN: 在说定的时刻，不拖延，从而守住约定或时刻表
senses.example: The train left promptly at seven.
senses.exampleCN: 火车七点整开走了。
senses.why: If readiness is the point, the sharpest display of it is being in place when the clock reaches the agreed mark, which is why the adverb also means punctually.
senses.whyCN: 如果要点是「随时可用」，那么最利落的展示就是钟点一到人已到位，所以这个副词也有「准时」之意。

senses.title: Without hesitation in answering or deciding
senses.definition: in a way that shows no hesitation, especially when agreeing, refusing or admitting something
senses.definitionCN: 表现出毫不迟疑，尤指在答应、拒绝或承认某事时
senses.example: He promptly agreed to take the night shift.
senses.exampleCN: 他干脆地答应上夜班。
senses.why: A ready answer is not only fast but unhedged; English lets the same adverb carry that firmness of a decision already made.
senses.whyCN: 现成的回答不仅快，而且不含糊；英语就让同一个副词承担这种「主意已定」的干脆。

intro.en: Promptly is an English-made adverb: the borrowed adjective prompt was simply given the native ending -ly, and the Latin picture of readiness came along with it.
intro.cn: promptly 是在英语内部造出的副词：借来的形容词 prompt 加上本族词尾 -ly，拉丁语「现成待用」的画面也一并跟了过来。

items.en: Emere meant to take or to buy, getting something into your hands.
items.cn: emere 意为拿取、购买，是把某物弄到手里。

items.en: Pro- plus emere gave promere, to bring something out into the open.
items.cn: pro- 加 emere 构成 promere，意为把东西拿到明处。

items.en: The participle promptus named what had been brought out, hence what is ready and quick to use.
items.cn: 分词 promptus 指已经被拿出来的东西，因此是现成、随时可用的。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective prompt from French and Latin, meaning ready and quick, and used it for both people and replies.
items.cn: 英语从法语和拉丁语借来形容词 prompt，意为现成而快速的，既用于人，也用于答复。

items.en: The native suffix -ly turned that adjective into an adverb of manner, so promptly means in a ready and immediate way.
items.cn: 本族词尾 -ly 把这个形容词变成方式副词，所以 promptly 意为「以现成、即刻的方式」。

note.en: The first group is the small English family around the adjective, including one formal noun; the second group gathers adverbs and near-synonyms of speed and timing.
note.cn: 第一组是围绕这个形容词的小词族，包括一个正式的名词；第二组收表示速度与时刻的副词及近义词。

entries.definition: The adjective and verb this adverb is built on: ready, quick, to urge.
entries.definitionCN: 这个副词所依附的形容词与动词：现成的、快的、促使。

entries.definition: The quality of being quick and punctual.
A formal noun for readiness and speed of action.
entries.definitionCN: 正式用语，指行动的敏捷与果断。

entries.definition: The act of cueing someone or nudging them to act.
entries.definitionCN: 给人提示或促使人行动的行为。

entries.definition: At a fast speed, with emphasis on how short the time is.
entries.definitionCN: 以很快的速度，强调时间之短。

entries.definition: At once, with no interval at all.
Exactly at the stated time.
Fast and smoothly, often with a literary tone.
entries.definitionCN: 又快又顺，常带文学色彩。

normalIntro.en: The adverb adds only a suffix to the adjective, so everything it means is the adjective's readiness turned into a way of acting.
normalIntro.cn: 这个副词只在形容词上加了一个词尾，所以它的全部含义都是把形容词的「现成」变成做事的方式。

normal.en: Prompt means ready at hand; add -ly and you get the manner of acting out of that readiness.
normal.cn: prompt 意为「就在手边待用」；加上 -ly，得到的就是从这份现成里长出的做事方式。

normal.en: Promptly at nine and promptly replied share one word because both show something already in place when needed.
normal.cn: promptly at nine 与 promptly replied 共用一个词，因为两者都表现出「需要时已经就位」。

normal.en: The -ly ending is native English, so promptly was made inside English rather than borrowed whole.
normal.cn: -ly 是英语本族词尾，所以 promptly 是在英语内部造出来的，而不是整体借来的。

normal.en: Promptitude is the formal cousin of promptness, both naming the same readiness as a quality.
normal.cn: promptitude 是 promptness 的正式近亲，两者都把同一份「现成」说成一种品质。

normal.en: Because it carries no hint of hurrying, promptly can describe calm efficiency rather than panic.
normal.cn: 由于它不带慌乱之意，promptly 可以形容从容的效率，而不是手忙脚乱。

abstract.en: Promptly measures the gap between needing something and having it, and tries to make that gap vanish.
abstract.cn: promptly 衡量的是「需要」与「到手」之间的空隙，并试图让这个空隙消失。

abstract.en: The same adverb covers speed and punctuality because both are forms of not keeping anyone waiting.
abstract.cn: 同一个副词兼指快与准时，因为两者都是「不让人等」的形式。

abstract.en: A prompt reply is a courtesy in grammar as well as in manners: it treats the other person's time as real.
abstract.cn: 迅速回复既是语法上的词，也是礼节上的事：它把别人的时间当真。

examples.en: She replied promptly to every message.
examples.cn: 她对每条消息都迅速回复。

examples.en: The meeting began promptly at nine.
examples.cn: 会议九点整准时开始。

examples.en: He promptly denied the rumour.
examples.cn: 他干脆地否认了那个传言。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普让普特利」——一催就动，动作快得带响；记住 promptly 是迅速地。

root: 由 prompt（迅速的；准时的）加副词后缀 -ly 构成；prompt 源自拉丁语 promere（拿出来）的分词 promptus（就在手边的），所以 promptly 的核心仍是「东西已在手边，动作立刻跟上」。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is acting out of readiness; the adverb then splits into speed, punctuality, and the firmness of a decision made without hedging.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「凭着现成而行动」；副词由此分出迅速、准时，以及不加含糊的果断。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the clock reaching the agreed mark while the person is already at the door, everything in hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：钟点刚到约定的那一格，人已站在门口，东西都在手上。

branches.en: a hand already raised before the question ends
branches.cn: 问题还没问完，手已经举起来

branches.en: a clock and a person arriving on the same beat
branches.cn: 钟点与人同时到位

branches.en: an answer that refuses to hedge
branches.cn: 毫不含糊的回答

branches.en: a letter written and posted in one morning
branches.cn: 同一个上午写完并寄出的信

branches.en: a quick yes given without a second thought
branches.cn: 不加犹豫就给出的答应

intro.en: The adverb is a Latin readiness carried by a French adjective and finished with a native English suffix.
intro.cn: 这个副词是拉丁语的「现成」，由法语形容词承载，再用英语本族词尾收尾。

latinIntro.en: Promptus, the participle of promere, is the reliable Latin cognate behind both prompt and promptly.
latinIntro.cn: promere 的分词 promptus 是 prompt 与 promptly 背后可靠的同源词。

definition_zh: 废除；废止；取消（法律、制度或习俗）
definition_en: to end a law, system or practice officially
core_image: 一份旧法令被盖上「作废」的印章
scene: 议会投票之后，延续百年的旧税制被正式取消。 The parliament voted to abolish the old tax.
sceneCN: 这里的 abolish 指「废除」（第 1 个义项：正式终止法律或制度）；句意是议会投票废除这项旧税。

derivatives.zh: 加 -ition 构成，义为「废除；废止」
义为「废奴主义者；主张废除者」

senses.title: To end a law officially
senses.definition: formally brings a law or rule to an end
senses.definitionCN: 正式使某项法律或规则终止
senses.example: The parliament voted to abolish the old tax.
senses.exampleCN: 议会投票废除了这项旧税。
senses.why: The Latin root means to wipe out, and a law wiped from the books no longer applies.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「抹去」，从法典里抹去的法律便不再生效。

senses.title: To end slavery
senses.definition: puts an end to the owning of people
senses.definitionCN: 终止蓄养人口的做法
senses.example: The movement to abolish slavery grew through the century.
senses.exampleCN: 废除奴隶制的运动在这一百年间壮大。
senses.why: The word's most famous use names the ending of an institution people had accepted.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最著名的用法，就是终结一项曾被人接受的制度。

senses.title: To cancel a fee
senses.definition: removes a charge or duty that people had to pay
senses.definitionCN: 取消人们原本必须缴纳的费用或税项
senses.example: The city decided to abolish the parking fee.
senses.exampleCN: 市政府决定取消停车费。
senses.why: A charge written into rules can be struck out like any other rule.
senses.whyCN: 写进规章的收费，可以像别的规章一样被划掉。

senses.title: To end a custom
senses.definition: stops a long-standing practice in a society
senses.definitionCN: 终止社会上长期存在的做法
senses.example: It is hard to abolish a custom that families keep privately.
senses.exampleCN: 要废止各家私下沿袭的习俗很难。
senses.why: Customs are unwritten laws, and the verb reaches them too.
senses.whyCN: 习俗是不成文的法，这个动词也能触及它们。

senses.title: To close an institution
senses.definition: ends the existence of an official body
senses.definitionCN: 使某个官方机构不再存在
senses.example: The reform will abolish two small agencies.
senses.exampleCN: 这项改革将撤销两个小机构。
senses.why: An institution exists by decree, so ending the decree ends the body.
senses.whyCN: 机构因法令而存在，终止法令便终止了机构。

senses.title: To end a punishment
senses.definition: removes a penalty from the legal code
senses.definitionCN: 从法典中取消某种刑罚
senses.example: Several states voted to abolish the death penalty.
senses.exampleCN: 几个州投票废除了死刑。
senses.why: A penalty is a clause in the code, and striking the clause abolishes it.
senses.whyCN: 刑罚是法典中的条款，删去条款就是废除。

senses.title: To drop a rule in sport
senses.definition: removes an old rule from the rules of a game
senses.definitionCN: 从比赛规则中删去旧条款
senses.example: The league voted to abolish the old offside rule.
senses.exampleCN: 联盟投票取消了旧的越位规则。
senses.why: Games are governed by written rules, and the word applies wherever rules are written.
senses.whyCN: 比赛由成文规则管理，凡有成文规则处都能用这个词。

senses.title: To annul a contract
senses.definition: in law, makes an agreement of no effect
senses.definitionCN: 法律上使某项协议失效
senses.example: The court may abolish the clause if it is unfair.
senses.exampleCN: 若条款不公，法院可废止该条款。
senses.why: Wiping out an obligation is the legal face of the same old idea.
senses.whyCN: 抹去一项义务，正是同一古老观念在法律上的面貌。

intro.en: The word goes back to a Latin verb meaning to wipe out.
intro.cn: 这个词可追溯到意为「抹去」的拉丁语动词。

items.en: abolisshen entered English with the sense of doing away with.
items.cn: abolisshen 进入英语，意为「取消、除去」。

note.cn: 形近组是 abolish 词族；近义组是别的表示「取消」的动词。

definition_en: an informal word for yes, used to agree, to answer a question, or to show that one is listening
core_image: 电话那头刚说完，这头随口应一声，表示听到了也同意了
scene: 朋友问要不要一起去吃面，另一个人一边拿外套一边随口答应。 Yeah, I will be there by seven.
sceneCN: 这里 yeah 是「是；对」（第 1 个义项：口语中表示同意或肯定的应答）；句意为「好，我七点前到」。电话那头随口应一声的样子，就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: The quick yes
senses.definition: a casual way of saying yes when agreeing to something or answering a question
senses.definitionCN: 同意某事或回答问题时随口说的「是」
senses.example: Yeah, I will be there by seven.
senses.exampleCN: 好，我七点前到。
senses.why: The word is simply yes pronounced loosely in fast speech, so the meaning of yes is kept whole.
senses.whyCN: 这个词就是 yes 在快说时松散的发音，所以 yes 的意思完整地保留了下来。

senses.title: The sound of listening
senses.definition: a short sound used to show that one is still listening or has understood
senses.definitionCN: 表示自己仍在听或已经明白的短促应声
senses.example: Yeah, yeah, go on, I am listening.
senses.exampleCN: 嗯，嗯，接着说，我在听。
senses.why: In talk, a quick yes also means that the message arrived, so the same sound becomes a signal of attention.
senses.whyCN: 在对话里，一声「是」也意味着信息收到了，于是同一个声音变成了注意力还在的信号。

senses.title: The doubtful yeah
senses.definition: said with a rising tone to show doubt or disbelief, often in yeah, right
senses.definitionCN: 用升调说出以示怀疑或不相信，常见于 yeah, right
senses.example: Yeah, right, and the bus just flew away.
senses.exampleCN: 是吗，然后公交车就飞走了吧。
senses.why: The same agreement word, said with the wrong tone, turns into its opposite, which is a common joke in English talk.
senses.whyCN: 同一个表示同意的小词，用错的语调说出来就变成了反话，这是英语口语里常见的玩笑。

senses.title: The answer to a call
senses.definition: used to answer when someone calls your name or knocks
senses.definitionCN: 别人叫你名字或敲门时的应答
senses.example: Yeah? Come in, the door is open.
senses.exampleCN: 哎？进来吧，门没锁。
senses.why: Answering a call with yes simply confirms that one is present, so the word serves as a doorbell reply.
senses.whyCN: 用「是」来应声，本质上就是确认自己在场，于是这个词成了门铃前的回答。

senses.title: The filler in speech
senses.definition: a long drawn-out yeah used while the speaker thinks, filling a pause in the sentence
senses.definitionCN: 说话人思考时拉长的一声「嗯」，用来填补句子中的停顿
senses.example: Yeah, well, it was not exactly what I meant.
senses.exampleCN: 嗯，这个嘛，那不是我的意思。
senses.why: A word that only signals agreement easily becomes a pause filler, so it can appear without agreeing to anything at all.
senses.whyCN: 一个只表示同意的小词很容易变成填充停顿的声音，于是它可以出现却并不真的同意什么。

intro.en: Yeah is a spoken form of yes, first written down in the nineteenth century to catch the way the word sounds in quick talk.
intro.cn: yeah 是 yes 的口语形式，到十九世纪才被写下来，为的是记下这个词在快说时的声音。

items.en: gēse was one of the emphatic forms of yes, built from the older word for so.
items.cn: 古英语 gēse 是 yes 的强调形式之一，由更古的「如此」一词构成。

items.en: The form reduced toward yes and yis in everyday speech.
items.cn: 中古英语时期，日常口语里逐渐简化为 yes、yis。

items.en: The stressed vowel weakened in informal talk, giving a sound like yeh.
items.cn: 在非正式谈话中重音元音弱化，产生了近似 yeh 的声音。

items.en: Editors began writing yeah in the nineteenth century to record dialogue in fiction.
items.cn: 十九世纪编辑开始用 yeah 记录小说中的对话。

items.en: Yeah is now the ordinary spoken agreement word, while yes stays the written and formal one.
items.cn: 如今 yeah 是口语中平常的同意词，yes 则保留书面与正式的用法。

note.en: Yeah belongs to a small family of spoken agreement words in English.
note.cn: yeah 属于英语口语中表示同意的一小族词。

scene: 球砸碎了窗户。 The ball smashed the window.

senses.title: Break violently
senses.definition: to break something into pieces with great force
senses.definitionCN: 用很大的力量把某物打碎
senses.example: The ball smashed the window.
senses.exampleCN: 球砸碎了窗户。
senses.why: This is the central physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心的身体动作义项。

senses.title: Hit hard

senses.exampleCN: 汽车猛地撞上了墙。
senses.why: The force can hit a surface as well as break it.
