sensesIntro.en: From the baked outside of bread, to any hard layer, to the shell of the earth.
sensesIntro.cn: 从面包烤硬的外层，到任何硬层，再到地球的外壳。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a warm loaf with a crisp brown shell.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只带着焦脆棕色外壳的热面包。

branches.en: The oven hardens the outside of the bread.
branches.cn: 炉火把面包的外层烤硬。

branches.en: Cold or salt can build a hard layer too.
branches.cn: 寒冷或盐也能结出一层硬壳。

branches.en: The whole planet rests inside one thin shell.
branches.cn: 整颗行星都包在一层薄壳里。

branches.en: Bread and ice both dry into a shell.
branches.cn: 面包与冰都干成一层壳。

branches.en: The same word covers a pond and a planet.
branches.cn: 同一个词既盖住池塘，也盖住行星。

intro.en: Crust brings a small family of words for hard outer layers and the things that wear them.
intro.cn: crust 带来一小族词，都与坚硬的外层以及披着外层的物有关。

latinIntro.en: The Latin crusta, a rind, is the root behind crust and crustacean.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 crusta（外皮）是 crust 与 crustacean 背后的根。

items.example: The bread has a dark crust.
items.exampleCN: 这面包有一层深色外皮。

items.example: The boots were crusted with mud.
She asked for a crustless sandwich.
items.exampleCN: 她要了一份去边的三明治。

items.meaning: to cover with a hard layer
to form a hard top layer
items.example: The snow crusted over at night.
items.exampleCN: 夜里雪面结了一层硬壳。

definition_en: shared by or involving a whole group of people, or a group that owns and runs something together
core_image: 一群人同时举起手，做出同一个决定
scene: 会议结束时，所有人一起点头通过方案。 The decision was a collective one, not a personal choice.
sceneCN: 这里 collective 指「集体的」（第 1 个义项：群体共同拥有的）；句意是这是集体的决定，而非个人的选择。

senses.title: Shared by a group
senses.definition: shared by or belonging to all members of a group
senses.definitionCN: 由群体全体成员共享或共有的
senses.example: The land is collective property.
senses.exampleCN: 这片土地是集体财产。
senses.why: The suffix -ive turns the act of gathering into a quality of the whole.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -ive 把聚拢的动作变成整体的性质。

senses.title: A group owning something together
senses.definition: a group of people who own and run something jointly
senses.definitionCN: 共同拥有并经营某事的群体
senses.example: The farmers formed a collective.
senses.exampleCN: 农民们成立了一个合作社。
senses.why: When people gather for a common good, the gathered group itself takes the name.
senses.whyCN: 当人们为共同利益聚在一起，聚成的群体本身也得了这个名字。

intro.en: Collective comes from Latin collectivus, from colligere, to gather.
intro.cn: collective 出自拉丁语 collectivus，源头是 colligere（聚拢）。

items.en: Colligere meant to gather into one place.
items.cn: colligere 意为聚到一处。

items.en: Collectivus described what belongs to a gathered whole.
items.cn: collectivus 描述属于聚成之整体的东西。

items.en: French collectif carried the adjective toward English.
items.cn: 法语 collectif 把这个形容词带向英语。

items.en: English collective first described shared duties.
items.cn: 英语 collective 最初描述共同的职责。

items.en: It also names farms and workplaces owned in common.
items.cn: 它还指共同拥有的农场与工作场所。

note.en: The look-alike group holds adjectives with similar endings, while the meaning group names what is held in common.
note.cn: 形近组收的是结尾相似的形容词，近义组列出共同拥有与共同参与。

entries.definition: worth keeping as part of a collection
meant to put something right
thinking carefully, or throwing back light
used or owned by more than one person
entries.definitionCN: 由不止一人使用或拥有的

entries.definition: done by two or more people together
entries.definitionCN: 由两方或多方一起完成的

entries.definition: belonging to a whole community

normalIntro.en: These hooks build the word from collect plus -ive, then split the shared quality from the group itself.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把它拆成 collect 加 -ive，再把共享性质与群体本身分开。

normal.en: Collect plus -ive gives the quality of a gathered whole.
normal.cn: collect 加 -ive，得到聚成整体所具有的性质。

normal.en: A collective decision needs more than one hand.
normal.cn: 集体的决定需要不止一只手。

normal.en: The noun form names the group, so a farm can be a collective.
normal.cn: 名词形式指这个群体，所以农场也能是一个集体。

normal.en: Collectively means everyone acting as one body.
normal.cn: collectively 意为所有人作为一个整体行动。

normal.en: Collectivism is the belief that the group comes first.
normal.cn: collectivism 是认为群体优先的信念。

abstract.en: Picture a room where every hand rises at the same moment.
abstract.cn: 想象一屋子人在同一刻举起手。

abstract.en: Picture a field worked by many families who share the harvest.
abstract.cn: 想象许多家庭共同耕种一块地，分享收成。

abstract.en: Picture one long table where everyone writes the same letter.
abstract.cn: 想象一张长桌，所有人一起写同一封信。

examples.en: The team made a collective decision to start again.
examples.cn: 团队做出了重新开始的集体决定。

examples.en: The village runs a collective that sells its own cheese.
examples.cn: 这个村子经营着一家出售自制奶酪的合作社。

examples.en: These memories are part of our collective past.
examples.cn: 这些记忆是我们共同过去的一部分。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 collective 记成 collect 加 ive：把大家的意见收在一起，就是集体的。

root: 源自拉丁语 collectivus，由 colligere（聚拢）派生，先指聚成整体的性质，后指共同经营的群体。

sensesIntro.en: First a quality shared by a whole, then the whole group that owns something.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是整体共享的性质，再是共同拥有某物的整体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one decision made by many hands at once.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个由许多只手同时做出的决定。

branches.en: The adjective sense describes what the group holds in common.
branches.cn: 形容词义描述群体共同拥有的东西。

branches.en: The noun sense turns that group into an organisation.
branches.cn: 名词义把这个群体变成一个组织。

branches.en: The quality and the body share one Latin root.
branches.cn: 性质与群体共享同一个拉丁词根。

branches.en: Collective memory belongs to no single person.
branches.cn: 集体记忆不属于任何单独的个人。

branches.en: A collective is a group that acts like one owner.
branches.cn: 合作社就是像一个所有者那样行动的群体。

intro.en: The family adds -ism, -ist and -ly to the base, and compounds such as collective farm.
intro.cn: 这个词族在词基上加 -ism、-ist 与 -ly，并有 collective farm 这类复合词。

latinIntro.en: Collectivus and colligere are the Latin sources, built on legere, to pick.
latinIntro.cn: collectivus 与 colligere 是拉丁语来源，建在 legere（挑选）之上。

items.example: Several collectives share the same market.
items.exampleCN: 几个合作社共用同一个市场。

items.meaning: as a group rather than as individuals
items.example: The staff collectively chose the name.
items.exampleCN: 全体员工共同选定了这个名字。

items.meaning: the belief that the group comes before the person
items.meaningCN: 认为群体先于个人的信念
items.example: The essay defended a mild collectivism.
items.exampleCN: 这篇文章为一种温和的集体主义辩护。

items.example: He held collectivist views in economics.
items.exampleCN: 他在经济上持集体主义观点。

items.meaning: the state of being a group
items.example: The law treats them as a collectivity.
items.exampleCN: 法律把他们视为一个整体。

items.meaning: a farm owned and worked by a group
items.meaningCN: 由群体拥有并耕种的农场
items.example: The collective farm shared its tools.

items.meaningCN: 整个社会共同记住的东西
items.example: The war lives on in collective memory.
items.exampleCN: 那场战争留在集体记忆里。

items.meaning: to bring property under group ownership
items.example: The state moved to collectivize the land.
items.exampleCN: 国家着手把土地收归集体。

latinEntries.example: Collectivus comes from the verb colligere.
Colligere is the base of the whole family.
latinEntries.exampleCN: colligere 是整个词族的根基。

definition_zh: 氧；氧气；空气中的氧；供呼吸用的氧气
definition_en: the chemical element that makes up about a fifth of the air, is needed for breathing and burning, and is supplied in cylinders for medical or high-altitude use
core_image: 看不见的气体让火苗忽然蹿高一截
scene: 清晨的树林里，叶子在阳光下无声地工作。 By midday the leaves had released enough oxygen into the clearing for a walker to feel the air turn fresh.
sceneCN: 这里要说明的是氧这种气体（第 1 个义项：空气中支持呼吸与燃烧的那种元素）；句意为到正午时，树叶已经把足够的气体释放到林间空地上，让散步的人觉得空气变清新了。图中可辨识物件：树叶、阳光、林间小路。

derivatives.zh: 由 oxygen 的词干 ox- 加化学后缀 -ide 构成，指氧与另一种元素组成的化合物
由词干 oxid- 加动词后缀 -ize 构成，指与氧化合、使生锈
由 oxygen 加动词后缀 -ate 构成，指给血液或水体供氧
由前缀 di-（二）加 oxide 构成，指含两个氧原子的化合物

senses.title: The element that makes up part of the air
senses.definition: the chemical element that forms about a fifth of the air and is needed for breathing and for burning
senses.definitionCN: 组成空气约五分之一的化学元素，呼吸和燃烧都离不开它
senses.example: Green plants give off oxygen during the day.
senses.exampleCN: 绿色植物在白天释放氧气。
senses.why: Greek oxys means sharp or sour and -genes means born or producing; the gas was named for the acids it was once thought to create.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 oxys 意为尖锐、酸，-genes 意为产生；人们曾以为这种气体能生成酸，命名就从此而来。

senses.title: A supply of the gas for breathing
senses.definition: the gas supplied in cylinders or through a mask so that people can breathe where the air is thin or unsafe
senses.definitionCN: 装在钢瓶里或经面罩供给的氧，用于空气稀薄或不宜呼吸的地方
senses.example: Climbers above eight thousand metres often breathe bottled oxygen.
senses.exampleCN: 八千米以上的登山者常常吸瓶装氧。
senses.why: As soon as oxygen names the gas itself, it can also name the measured amount of it that a hospital ward or a climber carries along.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 oxygen 指这种气体本身，也就能指医院病房或登山者随身携带的那一份定量供氧。

senses.title: The active part of air in burning and rusting
senses.titleCN: 氧（引起燃烧与生锈的成分）
senses.definition: the element thought of as the substance in air that combines with other materials when something burns or rusts
senses.definitionCN: 指空气里在燃烧或生锈时与其他物质结合的那种成分
senses.example: Oxygen in the damp air slowly turned the iron gate red with rust.
senses.exampleCN: 潮湿空气里的氧慢慢把铁门锈成了红色。
senses.why: Because the same gas makes a flame leap and makes iron decay, the word also names the partner hidden inside those two very different changes.
senses.whyCN: 因为同一种气体既能让火苗蹿起，也能让铁慢慢朽坏，所以这个词也指藏在这两种截然不同的变化背后的那一方。

intro.en: Oxygen is a scientific coinage of the late eighteenth century: two Greek roots were joined in French and then borrowed into English.
intro.cn: oxygen 是十八世纪后期造出的科学术语：两个希腊词根在法语里拼合，随后被英语借用。

items.en: Oxys meant sharp or sour, and the suffix -genes meant born or producing; together they described something that generates acid.
items.cn: oxys 意为尖锐、酸的，后缀 -genes 意为产生；两者合起来描述「能生成酸的东西」。

items.en: The French chemist Lavoisier and his colleagues are generally thought to have coined oxygène for the part of air they believed produced acids in combustion.
items.cn: 一般认为法国化学家拉瓦锡与同事造出 oxygène 一词，用来指他们所认为的、在燃烧中生成酸的那部分空气。

items.en: English adopted the French term as oxygen, and it quickly replaced the older vocabulary of phlogiston in chemical writing.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪九十年代借入法语术语，写作 oxygen，并很快在化学著作中取代了旧的燃素说法。

items.en: As chemistry settled, oxygen became the name of a single element, and compounds such as oxide and dioxide fixed the ox- stem.
items.cn: 随着化学体系定型，oxygen 成为一个元素的名称，oxide、dioxide 这类化合物词也固定了 ox- 这个词干。

items.en: Modern English uses oxygen for the gas in air, for bottled supplies in hospitals and aircraft, and loosely for anything a situation cannot do without.
items.cn: 现代英语里，oxygen 指空气中的氧、医院与飞机上的瓶装氧，也松散地指任何缺了就撑不下去的东西。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the other element names built with the same Greek ending; the near-meaning group gathers words for the air and for what we breathe.
note.cn: 形近组收其他用同一个希腊词尾构成的元素名；近义组收表示空气与呼吸的词。

entries.definition: The lightest element, named from Greek for water and the same -genes ending.
entries.definitionCN: 最轻的元素，由希腊语「水」加同一个 -genes 词尾构成。

entries.definition: The element that makes up most of the air, named from a root meaning soda.
entries.definitionCN: 占空气大部分的元素，名称来自表示碱的词根。

entries.definition: A compound in which oxygen is joined to another element.
entries.definitionCN: 氧与另一种元素结合形成的化合物。

entries.definition: A compound containing two atoms of oxygen in each molecule.
entries.definitionCN: 每个分子含两个氧原子的化合物。

entries.definition: The mixture of gases around us that we breathe.
entries.definitionCN: 我们周围可以呼吸的混合气体。

entries.definition: The layer of gases surrounding a planet.
entries.definitionCN: 包围一颗行星的气体层。

entries.definition: The air taken into and sent out of the lungs.
entries.definitionCN: 吸入与呼出肺部的空气。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Greek-rooted scientific label, and its whole family keeps the same two ideas: air and the making of acids or oxides.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是希腊词根造出的科学名称，整族词都围绕两个念头：空气，以及酸或氧化物的生成。

normal.en: Greek oxys means sharp or sour and -genes means producing, so the name literally says acid maker.
normal.cn: 希腊语 oxys 是尖锐、酸的，-genes 是产生，所以这个名字字面上就是「造酸者」。

normal.en: Oxygen takes about a fifth of the air by volume, while nitrogen takes most of the rest.
normal.cn: 按体积算，氧约占空气的五分之一，其余大部分是氮。

normal.en: Oxide and dioxide keep the ox- stem, and the ending -ide marks a compound of two elements.
normal.cn: oxide 与 dioxide 保留 ox- 词干，-ide 后缀表示两种元素组成的化合物。

normal.en: Oxidize and oxygenate are both verbs built on the same stem, one about combining with oxygen, the other about supplying it.
normal.cn: oxidize 与 oxygenate 都是同一词干上的动词，一个指与氧化合，一个指供给氧。

normal.en: An oxygen mask is simply the word turned into an object that fits over the face.
normal.cn: oxygen mask 只是把这个词变成一件罩在脸上的器物。

abstract.en: The gas that keeps a flame alive is also the gas that quietly eats iron, so the same power both feeds and destroys.
abstract.cn: 让火焰活下去的气体，也会悄悄吃掉铁；同一种力量既供养也销毁。

abstract.en: The name was built on a mistake about acids, yet it outlived the theory that produced it.
abstract.cn: 这个名字建立在关于酸的误解之上，却比产生它的理论活得更久。

abstract.en: Oxygen is invisible, and every breath is the moment it becomes visible as a need.
abstract.cn: 氧是看不见的，而每一次呼吸都是它作为「需要」显形的时刻。

examples.en: Green plants give off oxygen during the day.
examples.cn: 绿色植物在白天释放氧气。

examples.en: Climbers above eight thousand metres often breathe bottled oxygen.
examples.cn: 八千米以上的登山者常常吸瓶装氧。

examples.en: Oxygen in the damp air slowly turned the iron gate red with rust.
examples.cn: 潮湿空气里的氧慢慢把铁门锈成了红色。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥克斯精」——听成「奥克斯精华」，深吸一口，记住 oxygen 是氧。

root: 希腊语 oxys（尖锐、酸）加 -genes（产生），十八世纪法语据此造出 oxygène，再进入英语；同族词有 oxide、dioxide、oxidize。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the gas in the air that keeps breath and flame going; the senses then divide into the element itself, a bottled supply, and the active partner in burning and rust.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是空气里维持呼吸与火焰的那种气体；义项由此分为元素本身、瓶装供应，以及燃烧与生锈时参与反应的那一方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gas nobody can see, making a flame jump and a breath come easier.
core.cn: 核心意象：一种谁也看不见的气体，让火苗蹿高，也让呼吸顺畅。

branches.en: a leaf exchanging gas with the air at noon
branches.cn: 正午一片叶子与空气交换气体

branches.en: a candle burning brighter when fresh air moves in
branches.cn: 新鲜空气流入时蜡烛烧得更旺

branches.en: a climber breathing from a cylinder near the summit
branches.cn: 登山者在山顶附近吸钢瓶里的氧

branches.en: an iron gate turning red in wet weather
branches.cn: 铁门在潮湿天气里泛红

branches.en: a hospital bed with a mask resting on the pillow
branches.cn: 病床上搁着一只面罩

intro.en: The word is a modern scientific compound of two Greek pieces, and English suffixes then build the chemistry around it.
intro.cn: 这个词由两个希腊部件拼成的现代科学复合词，英语后缀随后在它周围建起一整套化学词汇。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; the term was coined in French from Greek roots, and the later scientific Latin form oxygenium is a modern borrowing of that coinage.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；术语是用法语从希腊词根造出的，后来科学拉丁语里的 oxygenium 只是对这一新造词的借用。

definition_en: to use up a resource, to eat or drink something, or to destroy something completely
core_image: 一张嘴把整盘食物吃空，盘子见了底
scene: 夏天的老空调整天开着，电表转得飞快。 Big cars consume far more fuel than small ones.
sceneCN: 这里 consume 指「消耗」（第 1 个义项：用掉资源或能量）；句意是大车比小车耗油多得多。

senses.title: Use up a resource
senses.definition: to use up energy, fuel or materials over time
senses.definitionCN: 在一段时间里用掉能量、燃料或材料
senses.example: Old machines consume too much electricity.
senses.exampleCN: 旧机器耗电太多。
senses.why: A resource is only noticed on the day it runs out.
senses.whyCN: 资源往往在耗尽那天才被人注意。

senses.title: Eat or drink
senses.definition: to eat or drink something until it is gone
senses.definitionCN: 把食物或饮料吃到、喝到不剩
senses.example: The guests consumed every dish on the table.
senses.exampleCN: 客人们把桌上的菜吃得精光。
senses.why: A meal is also a small act of using something up.
senses.whyCN: 一顿饭也是一次小小的用尽。

senses.title: Swallow up completely
senses.definition: to destroy something completely, especially by fire
senses.definitionCN: 彻底毁掉某物，尤指被火吞没
senses.example: The fire consumed the whole warehouse in minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 大火在几分钟内吞没了整座仓库。
senses.why: Fire takes without leaving anything on the plate.
senses.whyCN: 火拿走一切，盘子里什么也不剩。

intro.en: Consume comes from Latin consumere, to use up, built from com-, completely, and sumere, to take up.
intro.cn: consume 来自拉丁语 consumere，意为用尽，由 com-（彻底）与 sumere（拿取）构成。

items.en: Sumere meant to take up or take to oneself.
items.cn: sumere 意为拿起或取为己用。

items.en: Consumere meant to take up completely and so use up.
items.cn: consumere 意为彻底取走，因而用尽。

items.en: It also described fire taking a whole building.
items.cn: 它也描述火吞掉整座建筑。

items.en: French consumer kept the using and the destroying senses.
items.cn: 法语 consumer 同时保留耗用与毁掉两层意思。

items.en: English consume first meant to destroy or use up.
items.cn: 英语 consume 最初指毁掉或用尽。

items.en: It now commonly describes fuel, food and time.
items.cn: 如今它常用来描述燃料、食物与时间。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin take base sum-, and the meaning group names other verbs for using something up.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语拿取词基 sum-，近义组列出其他表示用尽的动词。

entries.definition: a person who buys goods or services
the act of using up fuel, food or time
to take something as true without proof
to put something to a purpose
to eat something very quickly or greedily
to use something until nothing is left

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from an empty plate, then move to a meter spinning fast and to a fire that leaves nothing.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一只空盘子开始，再到飞快转动的电表，最后到什么也不留的火。

normal.en: Con- is completely and sume is take, so consume is to take something completely away.
normal.cn: con- 是彻底，sume 是拿，consume 就是把东西彻底拿走。

normal.en: An empty plate is the clearest picture of consume.
normal.cn: 一只空盘子，是 consume 最清楚的画面。

normal.en: The meter spins because the machine consumes.
normal.cn: 电表飞转，是因为机器在消耗。

normal.en: Fire consumes; dinner consumes; a long meeting consumes your afternoon.
normal.cn: 火在吞噬，晚饭在被吃光，长会也在耗掉你的下午。

normal.en: What is consumed cannot be handed on.
normal.cn: 被消耗掉的东西，无法再交到别人手里。

abstract.en: Picture a fork scraping the last of a sauce.
abstract.cn: 想象一把叉子刮着盘底最后一点酱。

abstract.en: Picture a fuel gauge dropping toward empty.
abstract.cn: 想象油表向空位滑落。

abstract.en: Picture flame moving along a dry beam.
abstract.cn: 想象火焰顺着干燥的横梁蔓延。

examples.en: This heater consumes less power than the old one.
examples.cn: 这台取暖器比旧的省电。

examples.en: We consumed three pots of tea during the talk.
examples.cn: 谈话期间我们喝光了三壶茶。

examples.en: The flames consumed the dry grass in seconds.
examples.cn: 火焰几秒钟就吞没了干草。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 consume 记成 con（彻底）加 sume（拿取）：把东西彻底拿去用光，就是消耗、吃光。

root: 源自拉丁语 consumere（com 彻底 + sumere 拿取），本义是彻底取走，后指消耗资源、吃喝干净与吞噬烧毁。

sensesIntro.en: From fuel drained by a machine, to a table cleared by guests, and at last to a building swallowed by flame.
sensesIntro.cn: 从被机器耗掉的燃料，到被客人吃空的餐桌，最后到被火焰吞掉的建筑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plate scraped clean and a fuel gauge on empty.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只刮得干干净净的盘子，和一根见底的油表。

branches.en: The first sense is a slow drain that a meter can measure.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是电表能测出的缓慢流失。

branches.en: The second sense is eating and drinking until the dish is bare.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是吃到喝到盘碗空空。

branches.en: The third sense is destruction that leaves no remainder.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是不留残余的毁灭。

branches.en: Both senses turn something full into something less.
branches.cn: 两个义项都把满的东西变成更少的东西。

branches.en: Eating and burning are the same taking, only at different speeds.
branches.cn: 吃与烧是同一种拿取，只是速度不同。

intro.en: Consume is built on Latin com-, completely, plus sumere, to take up.
intro.cn: consume 由拉丁语 com-（彻底）与 sumere（拿取）构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin take base sum- also appears in assume, resume and presume.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的拿取词基 sum- 也出现在 assume、resume 与 presume 中。

items.meaning: to take something until it is gone
items.meaningCN: 一直拿取直到东西不剩

items.meaning: one who uses goods or services
items.example: The consumer asked for a refund.
Do not assume the door is locked.

items.meaning: to take something as likely before proof
items.example: I presume you have read the file.
items.exampleCN: 我猜你看过那份文件了。

items.meaning: to take one thing under a larger group
items.meaningCN: 把一物纳入更大的类别
items.example: These cases subsume several older rules.
items.exampleCN: 这些情形涵盖了若干旧规则。

definition_zh: 欢乐的；愉快的；喜庆的；微醺的
definition_en: cheerful and full of lively fun; also used of holidays and celebrations to wish joy, and in informal British use, pleasantly drunk
core_image: 壁炉火旺的冬夜，一家人围着桌子唱歌，窗上贴满手剪的雪花
scene: 壁炉里的柴火烧得正旺，窗上贴着手剪的雪花，孩子们正把彩纸环挂上门框。 The whole room felt merry as the family sang together.
sceneCN: 这里是「欢乐的、愉快的」（第 1 个义项：心情欢快）；句意为全家人一起唱歌时，整个屋子都显得喜气洋洋。图中可辨识物件：壁炉、纸雪花、彩纸环。

pos.zh: 欢乐的；愉快的；喜庆的；微醺的

derivatives.zh: 由 merry 去 y 加 -ment 构成，义为「欢乐；欢闹」
由 merry 去 y 加 -ly 构成，义为「欢快地；愉快地」
由 merry 与 making 复合而成，义为「欢庆；作乐」

senses.title: Cheerful and full of lively fun
senses.definition: cheerful, happy and full of lively fun, especially when people are together
senses.definitionCN: 高兴、快活、充满热闹的乐趣，尤指与人相处时
senses.example: The children grew merry as the music started.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐一响，孩子们就快活起来。
senses.why: Old English myrige meant pleasing and agreeable, so the earliest sense is not loud laughter but a mood that feels good to be inside.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 myrige 意为「令人愉快的、合意的」，所以最早的意思不是放声大笑，而是一种让人觉得舒服、愿意待在其中的心境。

senses.title: Lively and festive, as of a holiday
senses.definition: used of holidays and celebrations to wish someone joy, as in the fixed greeting for Christmas
senses.definitionCN: 用于节日与庆祝场合，向人道贺，如圣诞节的固定祝语
senses.example: They hung coloured lights and wished every neighbour a merry Christmas.
senses.exampleCN: 他们挂起彩灯，向每位邻居道一声圣诞快乐。
senses.why: Once a feast is a shared good time, the word attaches itself to the day rather than to the feeling, and ends up fixed inside holiday greetings.
senses.whyCN: 当宴饮成了众人共享的好时光，这个词就黏到日子本身上，而不只是心情，最后被固定进节日祝语里。

senses.title: Slightly drunk and cheerful
senses.definition: in informal British use, pleasantly drunk and therefore more talkative and cheerful than usual
senses.definitionCN: 英式口语中指喝得恰到好处、因而比平时更爱说笑的状态
senses.example: After two glasses of wine he was merry but still polite.
senses.exampleCN: 两杯酒下肚，他有了些酒意，却仍旧有礼。
senses.why: Drink lowers the guard, so the cheerfulness the word already names turns into the visible, glass-in-hand kind that loosens the tongue.
senses.whyCN: 酒放松了戒备，于是这个词本来就指的欢快，变成一种看得见、手上有杯子、会松开舌头的热闹。

intro.en: Merry belongs to the Germanic side of English and goes back to an Old English adjective meaning pleasing; no reliable Latin cognate is recorded for it.
intro.cn: merry 属于英语中的日耳曼语这一支，可追溯到意为「令人愉快的」的古英语形容词；它没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

items.en: A reconstructed adjective meaning agreeable or pleasant lay behind the word; scholars generally link it to a root for short, with the idea of time passing pleasantly.
items.cn: 这个词背后是一个重构的形容词，意为「合意的、令人愉快的」；一般认为它与表示「短」的词根有关，即时光短而愉快。

items.en: Myrige meant pleasing, delightful and agreeable, and it described places, sounds and company as much as people.
items.cn: myrige 意为令人愉快的、可爱的、合意的，既能形容人，也能形容地方、声音与同伴。

items.en: Middle English mery narrowed toward cheerful and lively, and the spelling settled on merry in the north.
items.cn: 中古英语的 mery 收窄为「快活、有生气」，拼写最终在北方定为 merry。

items.en: From the idea of a loosened, cheerful mood came the informal sense of pleasantly drunk, which stayed common in British speech.
items.cn: 从「心情松弛、快活」这一想法，引申出「微醺」的口语义，这个用法在英式英语中一直常见。

items.en: Modern English keeps merry mostly in fixed greetings and set phrases, while everyday cheerfulness is usually carried by other words.
items.cn: 现代英语里 merry 多保留在固定祝语与成语中，日常的「快活」通常由别的词来承担。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the merry family plus one word that only shares the sound; the near-meaning group collects words for cheer, jollity and celebration.
note.cn: 形近组收 merry 的词族，另加一个只是读音相近的词；近义组收表示快活、热闹与喜庆的词。

entries.definition: Lively fun and laughter shared by a group.
entries.definitionCN: 一群人共享的热闹与笑声。

entries.definition: In a cheerful, lively way.
The act of celebrating noisily and happily.
entries.definitionCN: 热热闹闹地庆祝的行为。

entries.definition: Only the sound is close; this verb means to become husband and wife, with no shared origin.
entries.definitionCN: 只是读音相近，这个词意为结婚，词源并不相同。

entries.definition: Showing good spirits, often as a steady habit rather than a burst of fun.
entries.definitionCN: 显得心情好，常是稳定的性情，而非一阵热闹。

entries.definition: Full of deep gladness, stronger and more inward than mere high spirits.
entries.definitionCN: 充满深切喜悦，比单纯兴致高更强烈、更内在。

entries.definition: Good-humoured and sociable, often with a hearty, slightly loud manner.
entries.definitionCN: 脾气温和、爱交际，常带爽朗而略响亮的派头。

entries.definition: Belonging to a feast or holiday, marked by decoration and celebration.
entries.definitionCN: 属于节庆的，以装点与庆祝为特征。

normalIntro.en: The word comes from an Old English adjective for what feels agreeable; its family keeps the shared good time, the laughter around it and the greetings it ended up inside.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词来自一个意为「令人觉得合意」的古英语形容词，同族词保留着共享的好时光、身旁的笑声，以及它最后被装进去的祝语。

normal.en: Myrige in Old English meant pleasing, so merry began as a good feeling rather than as noise.
normal.cn: 古英语 myrige 意为令人愉快，所以 merry 起初是一种好心情，而不是吵闹。

normal.en: The comparative is merrier, not more merry, because the word is short and old enough for the -er ending.
normal.cn: 比较级是 merrier 而不是 more merry，因为这个词又短又古老，够得上用 -er 词尾。

normal.en: Merriment adds -ment and turns the adjective into the shared state of being merry.
normal.cn: merriment 加 -ment，把形容词变成一种共享的「欢闹状态」。

normal.en: Merrily adds -ly, and the doubled r keeps the short e sound of merry.
normal.cn: merrily 加 -ly，双写的 r 保住了 merry 里短促的 e 音。

normal.en: Merry is now locked inside greetings such as Merry Christmas, which outlived most of its free uses.
normal.cn: merry 如今被锁在 Merry Christmas 这类祝语里，而这些祝语比它大多数自由用法活得更久。

abstract.en: A word for a pleasant mood ended up naming a whole season, which shows how a feeling can attach itself to a date on the calendar.
abstract.cn: 一个表示愉快心情的词最后指整个节季，这说明一种感受可以黏到日历上的某个日子上。

abstract.en: Merry lives mostly in greetings now, a reminder that some words survive by being said at the right moment.
abstract.cn: merry 如今多活在祝语里，提醒人有些词是靠「在对的时刻说出来」而存活的。

abstract.en: The same word can mean happy and slightly drunk, because both describe a guard that has been let down.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既能指快活又能指微醺，因为两者都描述一道被放下的戒备。

examples.en: The room grew merry as the fire caught and the singing began.
examples.cn: 火苗窜起、歌声响起时，屋子里渐渐欢腾起来。

examples.en: They wished the old man a merry Christmas and left a small parcel.
examples.cn: 他们祝老人圣诞快乐，留下一个小包裹。

examples.en: Two cups of hot wine made him merry enough to tell stories.
examples.cn: 两杯热酒下肚，他高兴得讲起了故事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「玛丽」——节日里人人喊着玛丽，满街欢腾；记住 merry 是欢乐的。

root: 古英语 myrige（令人愉快的）来自原始日耳曼语重构形式 *murgijaz，一般认为与表示「短」的词根有关，即时光短而愉快；细节仍有不同说法，无可靠拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a mood that feels good to be in; the senses spread to the festive day, the holiday greeting and the loosened cheer that comes with drink.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一种待着舒服的好心情；义项扩到喜庆的日子、节日祝语，以及酒意带来的松弛欢快。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fire burning high on a winter night, a family singing round the table, hand-cut snowflakes stuck to the window.
core.cn: 核心意象：冬夜壁炉火旺，一家人围着桌子唱歌，窗上贴满手剪的雪花。

branches.en: children laughing as the music starts
branches.cn: 音乐响起时笑成一团的孩子

branches.en: a table crowded with relatives and warm plates
branches.cn: 围满亲人、摆着热菜的桌子

branches.en: a paper greeting pinned above a door
branches.cn: 门楣上贴着的节日祝语

branches.en: two glasses on a table and a loosened tie
branches.cn: 桌上两只杯子与松开的领带

branches.en: a party where greetings and wine run together
branches.cn: 祝语与酒意混在一起的聚会

intro.en: The word is carried by an Old English adjective, its Middle English respelling, two English endings and a noun suffix; it has no reliable Latin cognate.
intro.cn: 这个词由古英语形容词、中古英语拼写、两个英语词尾与一个名词后缀共同支撑；它没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for merry: the word belongs to the Germanic branch, so the Latin side is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: merry 没有可靠的拉丁同族词，它属于日耳曼语这一支，因此拉丁同源部分留空。
